```{r}
# =============================================================================
# Full pattern annotation
#   1. Preranked GSEA on gene_spectra Z-scores (Hallmark, Reactome, GO:BP)
#   2. ORA on top 50 genes per pattern (GO:BP, one-sided hypergeometric)
# =============================================================================
organism         <- "Macaca mulatta"
n_top_genes_ora  <- 50
gsea_pval_cutoff <- 0.05
ora_pval_cutoff  <- 0.05

# Rhesus-mapped gene set collections
hallmark_sets <- msigdbr(species = organism, collection = "H") %>%
  split(x = .$gene_symbol, f = .$gs_name)
reactome_sets <- msigdbr(species = organism, collection = "C2", subcollection = "CP:REACTOME") %>%
  split(x = .$gene_symbol, f = .$gs_name)
gobp_sets <- msigdbr(species = organism, collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP") %>%
  split(x = .$gene_symbol, f = .$gs_name)

collapse_leading_edge <- function(df) {
  if ("leadingEdge" %in% colnames(df) && is.list(df$leadingEdge)) {
    df$leadingEdge <- vapply(df$leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";", FUN.VALUE = character(1))
  }
  df
}

cnmf_panel <- c(Invitro = paste0(output_dir, "PanelC_"),
                W2      = paste0(output_dir, "PanelD_"),
                D195    = paste0(output_dir, "PanelH_"),
                Pacute  = paste0(supp_dir,   "PanelA_"))

for (sample_name in names(sample_configs)) {
  cfg        <- sample_configs[[sample_name]]
  load_dir   <- cfg$load_dir
  run_name   <- cfg$run_name
  plot_name  <- cfg$plot_name
  selected_k <- cfg$selected_k
  panel_pfx  <- cnmf_panel[[sample_name]]

  cat("\n==========================================\n")
  cat("Annotating ", plot_name, " (K = ", selected_k, ")\n", sep = "")
  cat("==========================================\n")

  usage_file       <- file.path(load_dir, paste0(run_name, "_usage_K",        selected_k, ".csv"))
  spectra_file     <- file.path(load_dir, paste0(run_name, "_spectra_K",      selected_k, ".csv"))
  spectra_tpm_file <- file.path(load_dir, paste0(run_name, "_spectra_tpm_K",  selected_k, ".csv"))
  top_genes_file   <- file.path(load_dir, paste0(run_name, "_top_genes_K",    selected_k, ".csv"))

  if (!check_migrated(usage_file, spectra_file, spectra_tpm_file, top_genes_file,
                      cfg$rds)) next
  usage       <- read.csv(usage_file,       row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  spectra     <- read.csv(spectra_file,     row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  spectra_tpm <- read.csv(spectra_tpm_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  top_genes   <- read.csv(top_genes_file,   row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

  # --- UMAP: cNMF pattern weight per cell ---
  seurat_obj <- readRDS(cfg$rds)
  seurat_obj <- JoinLayers(seurat_obj, assay = "RNA")
  seurat_obj <- add_cnmf_to_seurat(seurat_obj, usage)
  fplot <- suppressMessages(
    FeaturePlot(seurat_obj, features = paste0("Pattern_", 1:selected_k), ncol = 4) &
      scale_color_viridis_c()
  )
  ggsave(fplot, file = paste0(panel_pfx, plot_name, "_cNMF_UMAP.pdf"),
         width = 16, height = 8)

  cat("\nTop 20 genes per pattern (by Z-score loading):\n")
  for (pat in colnames(spectra)) {
    pat_scores <- spectra[[pat]]
    names(pat_scores) <- rownames(spectra)
    top_20 <- names(sort(pat_scores, decreasing = TRUE))[1:20]
    cat(paste0("  ", pat, ": ", paste(top_20, collapse = ", "), "\n"))
  }

  # --- Preranked GSEA per pattern ---
  cat("\nRunning preranked GSEA (Hallmark)...\n")
  suppressWarnings(gsea_hallmark <- run_preranked_gsea(spectra, hallmark_sets, gsea_pval_cutoff))
  cat("Running preranked GSEA (Reactome)...\n")
  suppressWarnings(gsea_reactome <- run_preranked_gsea(spectra, reactome_sets, gsea_pval_cutoff))
  cat("Running preranked GSEA (GO:BP)...\n")
  suppressWarnings(gsea_gobp     <- run_preranked_gsea(spectra, gobp_sets,     gsea_pval_cutoff))

  cat("\nTop 5 Hallmark terms per pattern (by NES):\n")
  for (pat in colnames(spectra)) {
    pat_res <- gsea_hallmark[gsea_hallmark$pattern == pat, ]
    if (nrow(pat_res) == 0) { cat(paste0("  ", pat, ": no significant terms\n")); next }
    pat_res <- pat_res[order(abs(pat_res$NES), decreasing = TRUE), ]
    top_terms <- head(pat_res, 5)
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(top_terms))) {
      direction <- ifelse(top_terms$NES[j] > 0, "+", "-")
      term <- gsub("^HALLMARK_", "", top_terms$pathway[j])
      cat(sprintf("  %s: [%s] %s (NES=%.2f, padj=%.1e)\n",
                  pat, direction, term, top_terms$NES[j], top_terms$padj[j]))
    }
  }

  # --- ORA per pattern (top 50 genes, GO:BP, hypergeometric) ---
  top50_per_pattern <- get_top_n_genes(spectra, n = n_top_genes_ora)
  background <- rownames(spectra)

  cat("\nRunning ORA on top", n_top_genes_ora, "genes per pattern (GO:BP)...\n")
  ora_results <- list()
  for (pat in names(top50_per_pattern)) {
    ora_results[[pat]] <- run_ora_hypergeometric(
      query_genes      = top50_per_pattern[[pat]],
      gene_sets        = gobp_sets,
      background_genes = background,
      pval_cutoff      = ora_pval_cutoff
    )
  }

  cat("\nTop 5 ORA GO:BP terms per pattern:\n")
  for (pat in names(ora_results)) {
    res <- ora_results[[pat]]
    if (nrow(res) == 0) { cat(paste0("  ", pat, ": no significant terms\n")); next }
    top_terms <- head(res, 5)
    for (j in seq_len(nrow(top_terms))) {
      cat(sprintf("  %s: %s (padj=%.1e, %d/%d genes)\n",
                  pat, gsub("^GOBP_", "", top_terms$pathway[j]),
                  top_terms$padj[j], top_terms$overlap[j], n_top_genes_ora))
    }
  }

  # --- Plot: GSEA Hallmark NES heatmap ---
  if (nrow(gsea_hallmark) > 0) {
    nes_matrix <- gsea_hallmark %>%
      select(pattern, pathway, NES) %>%
      mutate(pathway = gsub("^HALLMARK_", "", pathway)) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = pattern, values_from = NES, values_fill = 0) %>%
      tibble::column_to_rownames("pathway")
    nes_mat <- as.matrix(nes_matrix)
    max_abs <- max(abs(nes_mat), na.rm = TRUE)
    p_hallmark <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
      nes_mat,
      color        = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
      breaks       = seq(-max_abs, max_abs, length.out = 101),
      cluster_cols = TRUE, cluster_rows = TRUE,
      fontsize_row = 7, fontsize_col = 10,
      main         = paste0(plot_name, " GSEA Hallmark NES per cNMF pattern"),
      silent       = TRUE
    )
    ggsave(file.path(supp_dir, paste0(plot_name, "_cNMF_gsea_hallmark_heatmap.pdf")),
           plot = p_hallmark, width = 10, height = max(6, nrow(nes_mat) * 0.25))
    cat("\nSaved Hallmark GSEA heatmap.\n")
  }

  # --- Save GSEA/ORA CSVs to SuppFig3 ---
  write.csv(collapse_leading_edge(gsea_hallmark),
            file.path(supp_dir, paste0(plot_name, "_gsea_hallmark_results.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(collapse_leading_edge(gsea_reactome),
            file.path(supp_dir, paste0(plot_name, "_gsea_reactome_results.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(collapse_leading_edge(gsea_gobp),
            file.path(supp_dir, paste0(plot_name, "_gsea_gobp_results.csv")),     row.names = FALSE)

  ora_combined <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ora_results), function(pat) {
    df <- ora_results[[pat]]
    if (nrow(df) > 0) df$pattern <- pat
    df
  }))
  if (!is.null(ora_combined) && nrow(ora_combined) > 0) {
    write.csv(ora_combined,
              file.path(supp_dir, paste0(plot_name, "_ora_gobp_results.csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  }

  top50_df <- data.frame(
    lapply(top50_per_pattern, function(x) { length(x) <- n_top_genes_ora; x }),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  write.csv(top50_df,
            file.path(supp_dir, paste0(plot_name, "_top50_genes_per_pattern.csv")), row.names = FALSE)

  cat("Annotation outputs for", plot_name, "saved to:", supp_dir, "\n")
}
```

Program names below come from one shared basis across the four per-sample
cNMF runs, so a program that recurs in several samples carries the same name.
The similarity heatmap behind it is SuppFig3 cNMF_metaprogram_similarity.pdf.




### Panels C, D, H: enrichment

Enrichment dot plots and violins. Four contrasts per panel, two of which carry
into the figure:

  - `SIV+ vs SIV-`, every uninfected cell as reference (figure)
  - `SIV+ vs SIV-`, uninfected cells matched on host library size decile
  - `splice+ vs splice-`, unadjusted (figure)
  - `splice+ vs splice-`, viral burden held fixed

Host library size is matched on rather than regressed out, and enters the splice
contrast not at all. The tests behind that choice are in SuppFigs.Rmd:
`suppfig3_depth_confounding`, before Supp Fig 3 Panel B, for the two detection
tests, and `suppfig2_panelF_depth`, after Supp Fig 2 Panel F, for the splice one.

Prerequisite: the cleaned cNMF run for each sample, i.e. the second pass from
`extractionScripts/submissionScripts/Figure3/cNMF_subpattern.sh` followed by
`cNMF_postprocess.sh <run_name> <K>`. The K each cleaned run was taken to is in
`cNMF_subpattern.csv` and is written into the usage filename the chunk below
reads.

```{r}
combined_dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/dataframes/")
output_dir   <- paste0(plot.root, "Figure3/")
supp_dir     <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig3/")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(supp_dir,   recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# -log10(adj. p) cap 
p_scale_cap <- 10

# Host library size per cell
coords_dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                     "singleCell/Seurat/UMAPcoords/")

enrichment_panels <- list(
  list(
    panel      = "PanelC_Invitro",
    usage_file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                        "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/Invitro_cleaned_usage_K5.csv"),
    tables     = c("Invitro_all.csv"),
    coords     = c("InvitroUMAP_coords.csv"),
    pattern_labels = cnmf_metaprogram_labels$Invitro,
    out_dir    = output_dir
  ),
  list(
    panel      = "PanelD_W2",
    usage_file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                        "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/W2_cleaned_usage_K7.csv"),
    tables     = c("W2_all.csv"),
    coords     = c("W2UMAP_coords.csv"),
    pattern_labels = cnmf_metaprogram_labels$W2,
    out_dir    = output_dir
  ),
  list(
    panel      = "PanelH_D195",
    usage_file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                        "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/D195_cleaned_usage_K6.csv"),
    tables     = c("D195_all.csv"),
    coords     = c("D195UMAP_coords.csv"),
    pattern_labels = cnmf_metaprogram_labels$D195,
    out_dir    = output_dir
  ),
  list(
    panel      = "PanelA_Pacute",
    usage_file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                        "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/Pacute_cleaned_usage_K6.csv"),
    tables     = c("Pacute_all.csv"),
    coords     = c("PacuteUMAP_coords.csv"),
    pattern_labels = cnmf_metaprogram_labels$Pacute,
    out_dir    = supp_dir
  )
)

# Pass 1: every comparison for every panel, nothing drawn yet.
enrichment_results <- list()
for (cfg in enrichment_panels) {
  if (!check_migrated(cfg$usage_file)) next
  usage <- read.csv(cfg$usage_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

  all <- bind_rows(lapply(cfg$tables, function(f) read.csv(paste0(combined_dir, f))))

  infected <- all %>% filter(total > 0)
  infected_cellids <- infected$cellID

  splice_cols <- siv_splice_cols(infected)
  splice_pos_cellids <- infected %>%
    filter(if_any(all_of(splice_cols), ~ . > 0)) %>%
    pull(cellID)
  splice_neg_cellids <- setdiff(infected_cellids, splice_pos_cellids)
  if (length(splice_pos_cellids) < 3 || length(splice_neg_cellids) < 3) {
    cat("Skipping", cfg$panel, "- splice+", length(splice_pos_cellids),
        "splice-", length(splice_neg_cellids), "\n"); next
  }

  infected_comparison <- compare_pattern_usage(usage, infected_cellids)
  splicing_comparison <- compare_pattern_usage(usage, splice_pos_cellids,
                                               splice_neg_cellids,
                                               group_labels = c("splice_pos", "splice_neg"))

  # splice+ vs splice- at fixed viral burden. Burden is what decides whether a
  # spliced UMI is seen, so it confounds the splice call and is held fixed; host
  # library size does not predict splice status once burden is in the model
  # (see compare_pattern_usage_adjusted) and is left out.
  burden_cols <- setdiff(colnames(infected),
                         c("cellID", "UMAP1", "UMAP2", "cluster", "total"))
  burden_covariates <- data.frame(
    log_burden = log1p(rowSums(infected[, burden_cols, drop = FALSE])),
    row.names  = as.character(infected$cellID))
  splicing_comparison_adj <- compare_pattern_usage_adjusted(
    usage, splice_pos_cellids, splice_neg_cellids,
    covariates = burden_covariates,
    group_labels = c("splice_pos", "splice_neg"))

  # SIV+ vs SIV- against uninfected cells matched on host library size decile.
  # The size gap between infected and uninfected cells is a property of infected
  # cells rather than a detection artifact, so it is matched on rather than
  # regressed out (see compare_pattern_usage_matched).
  size_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(cfg$coords, function(f)
    read.csv(paste0(coords_dir, f))[, c("cellID", "size")]))
  host_size <- setNames(size_tab$size, as.character(size_tab$cellID))
  infected_comparison_matched <- compare_pattern_usage_matched(
    usage, infected_cellids, match_values = host_size)

  enrichment_results[[cfg$panel]] <- list(
    cfg = cfg,
    comparisons = list(
      list(result = infected_comparison,
           label  = "SIV+ vs SIV-",
           colors = c("#E41A1C", "gray70"), figure = TRUE),
      list(result = infected_comparison_matched,
           label  = "SIV+ vs SIV-\n(depth-matched)",
           colors = c("#E41A1C", "gray70"), figure = FALSE),
      list(result = splicing_comparison,
           label  = "splice+ vs splice-",
           colors = c("purple", "orange"), figure = TRUE),
      list(result = splicing_comparison_adj,
           label  = "splice+ vs splice-\n(burden controlled)",
           colors = c("purple", "orange"), figure = FALSE)
    ))

  cat("\n", cfg$panel, ": SIV+", length(infected_cellids),
      "| splice+", length(splice_pos_cellids), "| splice-", length(splice_neg_cellids), "\n")
  print(merge(infected_comparison$comparison,
              infected_comparison$stats[, c("pattern", "p_adj")], by = "pattern"))
  cat("  SIV+ vs SIV-, host library size decile matched (",
      infected_comparison_matched$n_cells["group1"], "vs",
      infected_comparison_matched$n_cells["group2"], "cells):\n")
  print(merge(infected_comparison_matched$comparison,
              infected_comparison_matched$stats[, c("pattern", "p_adj")], by = "pattern"))
  print(merge(splicing_comparison$comparison,
              splicing_comparison$stats[, c("pattern", "p_adj")], by = "pattern"))
  cat("  splice+ vs splice-, viral burden controlled (",
      splicing_comparison_adj$n_cells["group1"], "vs",
      splicing_comparison_adj$n_cells["group2"], "cells):\n")
  print(merge(splicing_comparison_adj$comparison,
              splicing_comparison_adj$stats[, c("pattern", "adjusted_difference", "p_adj")],
              by = "pattern"))
}

# Shared colour limits. Within a panel the two rows of a contrast already share
# one scale (they are drawn in the same colours), and taking the maximum across
# panels puts all four on one scale, so a colour means the same fold change
# wherever it appears. Contaminant programs are excluded here exactly as the
# plot excludes them: a degenerate fold change in one would otherwise set the
# limit for every panel.
enrichment_limits <- function(results, rows) {
  lims <- purrr::map_dfr(results, function(res) {
    keep <- names(res$cfg$pattern_labels)[
      !grepl("contaminant|contamination", res$cfg$pattern_labels, ignore.case = TRUE)]
    purrr::map_dfr(res$comparisons[rows(res$comparisons)], function(entry)
      entry$result$comparison %>%
        filter(pattern %in% keep) %>%
        transmute(group = sub("\n.*", "", entry$label),
                  fc    = abs(log2_fold_change)))
  }) %>%
    group_by(group) %>%
    summarise(limit = max(fc[is.finite(fc)]), .groups = "drop")
  setNames(lims$limit, paste0("log2 FC, ", lims$group))
}
is_figure_row <- function(comparisons) vapply(comparisons, `[[`, logical(1), "figure")

# The figure panels carry two of the four rows, so their colours are scaled to
# that range rather than to the wider one the supplement spans.
fc_limits_all    <- enrichment_limits(enrichment_results, function(x) rep(TRUE, length(x)))
fc_limits_figure <- enrichment_limits(enrichment_results, is_figure_row)
cat("\nShared log2 FC limits, all contrasts (supplement):\n"); print(round(fc_limits_all, 2))
cat("Shared log2 FC limits, figure rows only (Figure 3):\n"); print(round(fc_limits_figure, 2))

# Pass 2: the figure panel (controlled rows) and the supplemental version
# (every contrast), each on its own shared scale.
enrichment_plots <- list()
for (res in enrichment_results) {
  enrichment_plots[[res$cfg$panel]] <- plot_pattern_enrichment(
    comparisons    = res$comparisons[is_figure_row(res$comparisons)],
    output_prefix  = paste0(res$cfg$out_dir, res$cfg$panel, "_cNMF_enrichment"),
    styles         = "dots",
    pattern_labels = res$cfg$pattern_labels,
    max_neglog10_p = p_scale_cap,
    fc_limits      = fc_limits_figure)$dots

  plot_pattern_enrichment(
    comparisons    = res$comparisons,
    output_prefix  = paste0(supp_dir, sub("^Panel[A-Z]_", "", res$cfg$panel),
                            "_cNMF_enrichment_allContrasts"),
    styles         = "dots",
    pattern_labels = res$cfg$pattern_labels,
    max_neglog10_p = p_scale_cap,
    fc_limits      = fc_limits_all)
}


## violins
combined_dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/dataframes/")
output_dir   <- paste0(plot.root, "Figure3/")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

subset_panels <- list(
  Invitro = list(
    usage_file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                        "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/Invitro_cleaned_usage_K5.csv"),
    tables     = c("Invitro_all.csv")
  ),
  W2 = list(
    usage_file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                        "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/W2_cleaned_usage_K7.csv"),
    tables     = c("W2_all.csv")
  ),
  D195 = list(
    usage_file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                        "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/D195_cleaned_usage_K6.csv"),
    tables     = c("D195_all.csv")
  )
)

for (plot_name in names(subset_panels)) {
  cfg   <- subset_panels[[plot_name]]
  if (!check_migrated(cfg$usage_file)) next
  usage <- read.csv(cfg$usage_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

  all <- bind_rows(lapply(cfg$tables, function(f) read.csv(paste0(combined_dir, f))))

  infected <- all %>% filter(total > 0)
  infected_cellids <- infected$cellID

  # SIV+ vs SIV-
  comparison <- compare_pattern_usage(usage, infected_cellids)
  plot_pattern_violins(comparison, paste0(output_dir, plot_name, "_cNMF_infected_violins.pdf"),
                       colors = c("#E41A1C", "gray70"))

  # splice+ vs splice-
  splice_cols <- siv_splice_cols(infected)
  splice_pos <- infected %>%
    filter(if_any(all_of(splice_cols), ~ . > 0))
  splice_pos_cellids <- splice_pos$cellID
  splice_neg_cellids <- setdiff(infected_cellids, splice_pos_cellids)

  if (length(splice_pos_cellids) == 0) {
    cat("Skipping", plot_name, "-- no cells SIV+splice+\n")
  } else {
    comparison <- compare_pattern_usage(usage, splice_pos_cellids, splice_neg_cellids,
                                        group_labels = c("splice_pos", "splice_neg"))
    plot_pattern_violins(comparison, paste0(output_dir, plot_name, "_cNMF_splicing_violins.pdf"),
                         group_names = c("splice_pos", "splice_neg"),
                         colors = c("purple", "orange"))
    cat("Saved plots:", plot_name, "\n")
  }
}
```



### Panel F: splice+ and viral transcript load

Prerequisite: the `tier_tables` chunk has written `<sample>_tiers.csv`.

```{r panelF_splice_burden}
tier_table.dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/")
output.dir     <- paste0(plot.root, "Figure3/")
dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

panelF_samples <- c(Invitro = "in vitro", W2 = "viremia (W2)")
panelF_pal <- setNames(c("#594A42", "#EE2A7B"), unname(panelF_samples))

# Bins break at 8, the `tier_binload_cut` of Panel C, so that panel's low (2-7)
# and high (8+) load groups can be read straight off this axis; above the break
# bins double in width, so the x axis stays even on a log scale. A bin holding
# fewer cells than this carries no usable rate.
panelF_bins <- c(0, 2, 4, 7, 16, 32, 64, 128, Inf)
panelF_bin_labels <- c("1-2", "3-4", "5-7", "8-16", "17-32", "33-64", "65-128", ">128")
panelF_min_cells <- 10

panelF_cells <- bind_rows(lapply(names(panelF_samples), function(sample_name) {
  read.csv(paste0(tier_table.dir, sample_name, "_tiers.csv")) %>%
    filter(care_UMIs > 0) %>%
    transmute(sample = factor(panelF_samples[sample_name], levels = unname(panelF_samples)),
              cellID = as.character(cellID), care_UMIs, care_spliced)
})) %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(care_UMIs, panelF_bins, labels = panelF_bin_labels))

panelF_rate <- panelF_cells %>%
  group_by(sample, bin) %>%
  summarise(cells = n(), splice_pos = sum(care_spliced), rate = mean(care_spliced),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(cells >= panelF_min_cells)
print(as.data.frame(panelF_rate))

panelF_distribution <- panelF_cells %>%
  count(sample, bin) %>%
  group_by(sample) %>% mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()

# Per-sample splice+ rate standardised to the other sample's burden
# distribution, splitting the observed gap into the share the burden shift
# carries and the share left at matched burden.
panelF_standardise <- function(rate_sample, distribution_sample) {
  rates <- panelF_rate %>% filter(sample == rate_sample) %>% select(bin, rate)
  weights <- panelF_distribution %>% filter(sample == distribution_sample) %>% select(bin, frac)
  full_join(rates, weights, by = "bin") %>%
    filter(!is.na(frac)) %>%
    mutate(rate = ifelse(is.na(rate), 0, rate)) %>%
    summarise(value = sum(rate * frac)) %>% pull(value)
}
panelF_observed <- panelF_cells %>% group_by(sample) %>%
  summarise(cells = n(), splice_pos = sum(care_spliced), rate = mean(care_spliced),
            ge32 = mean(care_UMIs >= 32), q90 = quantile(care_UMIs, 0.9), .groups = "drop")
print(as.data.frame(panelF_observed))
cat(sprintf(
  "gap %.1f points; W2 rates on in vitro burden %.1f%% (burden shift %.1f points, %.0f%%); in vitro rates on W2 burden %.1f%% (residual %.1f points, %.0f%%)\n",
  100 * diff(rev(panelF_observed$rate)),
  100 * panelF_standardise("viremia (W2)", "in vitro"),
  100 * (panelF_standardise("viremia (W2)", "in vitro") - panelF_observed$rate[2]),
  100 * (panelF_standardise("viremia (W2)", "in vitro") - panelF_observed$rate[2]) /
    diff(rev(panelF_observed$rate)),
  100 * panelF_standardise("in vitro", "viremia (W2)"),
  100 * (panelF_standardise("in vitro", "viremia (W2)") - panelF_observed$rate[2]),
  100 * (panelF_standardise("in vitro", "viremia (W2)") - panelF_observed$rate[2]) /
    diff(rev(panelF_observed$rate))))

# The curves are labelled in place, so neither panel carries a colour legend.
panelF_curve_labels <- data.frame(
  sample    = factor(unname(panelF_samples), levels = unname(panelF_samples)),
  x         = c(2.5, 4.4),
  y         = c(0.93, 0.40),
  fontface  = c("italic", "plain"))

panelF_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black"),
        axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black"),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
        legend.position = "right")

panelF_rate_plot <- ggplot(panelF_rate, aes(bin, rate, color = sample, group = sample)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(size = cells)) +
  geom_text(data = panelF_curve_labels,
            aes(x, y, label = sample, color = sample, fontface = fontface),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = panelF_pal, guide = "none") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, name = "cells") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1),
                     breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "splice+ (% of cells in bin)") +
  panelF_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.line.x = element_blank())

panelF_distribution_plot <- ggplot(panelF_distribution, aes(bin, frac, fill = sample)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = panelF_pal, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Ca*Re viral UMIs per cell", y = "cells (% of sample)") +
  panelF_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave(paste0(output.dir, "PanelF_spliceRate_vs_burden.pdf"),
       panelF_rate_plot / panelF_distribution_plot + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1)),
       width = 5.5, height = 6)
```

### Gene-level concordance
Whole-sample Ca*Re-only cells against each TenX reference contrast in
`tier_reference_contrasts`, over the genes both contrasts tested: `GEX_vs_neg`
(every TenX-positive cell) and `Both_vs_neg` (the cells both chemistries call, so
no GEX call rests on the TenX arm's thresholds alone). Each gene is classed as
`shared` (significant in both, same sign), `discordant` (both, opposite sign),
`GEX only`, `Ca*Re-added only`, or `ns`. For the reference DEGs: the fraction
whose fold change has the same sign in the Ca*Re-only cells (binomial test
against 0.5); for `GEX_vs_neg`, how much of their fold change survives in
`GEX_naive` (median ratio of |log2FC|, paired Wilcoxon on |log2FC|). A
Ca*Re-added-only gene is traced to its likely source:
`fraction_significant_matched_n` from the downsampled draws, and
`in_GEX_untestable_cluster` if it is significant in `CaReOnly_vs_neg` inside a
cluster where the reference contrast was skipped for cell count.
Writes `<sample>_<reference>_gene_classes.csv`.
Prerequisites: the `tier_tables` and `tier_deg` chunks; `tier_downsample` for the
matched-n column.
```{r tier_concordance, warning=FALSE}
deg.dir   <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/DEG/tiers/")
table.dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/")
samples   <- c("Invitro", "W2", "Pacute", "D195")
# DEG call thresholds, as in the tier_deg chunk that wrote the tables
fc_threshold   <- 0.5
pval_threshold <- 0.01
reference_contrasts <- c(GEX_vs_neg = "TenX-positive", Both_vs_neg = "both")
tiers_all <- read_tier_tables(table.dir, samples)

tier_is_significant <- function(padj, log2FC) padj < pval_threshold & abs(log2FC) > fc_threshold

tier_concordance_one <- function(sample_name, reference_contrast) {
  reference_label <- reference_contrasts[[reference_contrast]]
  tenx   <- tier_read_deg(deg.dir, sample_name, "all", reference_contrast)
  care  <- tier_read_deg(deg.dir, sample_name, "all", "CaReOnly_vs_neg")
  naive <- if (reference_contrast == "GEX_vs_neg") {
    tier_read_deg(deg.dir, sample_name, "all", "GEX_naive")
  } else NULL
  if (is.null(tenx) || is.null(care)) {
    cat("Skipping", sample_name, "-", reference_contrast,
        "or CaReOnly_vs_neg not tested\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  genes <- inner_join(
    tenx  %>% select(gene, gex_log2FC  = avg_log2FC, gex_padj  = p_val_adj),
    care %>% select(gene, care_log2FC = avg_log2FC, care_padj = p_val_adj),
    by = "gene") %>%
    mutate(gex_sig   = tier_is_significant(gex_padj, gex_log2FC),
           care_sig  = tier_is_significant(care_padj, care_log2FC),
           same_sign = sign(gex_log2FC) == sign(care_log2FC),
           class = case_when(gex_sig & care_sig & same_sign ~ "shared",
                             gex_sig & care_sig             ~ "discordant",
                             gex_sig                        ~ "GEX only",
                             care_sig                       ~ "Ca*Re-added only",
                             TRUE                           ~ "ns"))

  downsampled_file <- paste0(deg.dir, sample_name, "_CaReOnly_vs_neg_downsampled.csv")
  genes$fraction_significant_matched_n <- if (file.exists(downsampled_file)) {
    downsampled <- read.csv(downsampled_file)
    downsampled$fraction_significant[match(genes$gene, downsampled$gene)]
  } else NA_real_

  tests <- read.csv(paste0(deg.dir, sample_name, "_tests.csv"))
  untestable_clusters <- tests %>%
    filter(scope != "all", contrast %in% c(reference_contrast, "CaReOnly_vs_neg")) %>%
    select(scope, contrast, tested) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = contrast, values_from = tested) %>%
    filter(!.data[[reference_contrast]], CaReOnly_vs_neg) %>%
    pull(scope)
  cluster_hits <- unique(unlist(lapply(untestable_clusters, function(scope) {
    deg <- tier_read_deg(deg.dir, sample_name, scope, "CaReOnly_vs_neg")
    deg$gene[tier_is_significant(deg$p_val_adj, deg$avg_log2FC)]
  })))
  genes$in_GEX_untestable_cluster <- genes$gene %in% cluster_hits

  if (!is.null(naive)) {
    genes <- genes %>%
      left_join(naive %>% select(gene, naive_log2FC = avg_log2FC), by = "gene")
  } else genes$naive_log2FC <- NA_real_

  write.csv(genes, paste0(deg.dir, sample_name, "_", reference_contrast,
                          "_gene_classes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

  tenx_deg <- genes %>% filter(gex_sig)
  diluted <- tenx_deg %>% filter(!is.na(naive_log2FC))
  care_added <- genes %>% filter(class == "Ca*Re-added only")

  tibble(
    sample = sample_name,
    reference = reference_contrast,
    n_genes_tested   = nrow(genes),
    spearman_log2FC  = cor(genes$gex_log2FC, genes$care_log2FC, method = "spearman"),
    n_GEX_DEG        = nrow(tenx_deg),
    n_CaRe_only_DEG  = sum(genes$care_sig),
    n_shared         = sum(genes$class == "shared"),
    n_discordant     = sum(genes$class == "discordant"),
    n_GEX_only       = sum(genes$class == "GEX only"),
    n_CaRe_added_only  = nrow(care_added),
    pct_TenX_DEG_same_sign = if (nrow(tenx_deg) > 0)
      round(100 * mean(tenx_deg$same_sign), 1) else NA_real_,
    p_same_sign_binomial = if (nrow(tenx_deg) > 0)
      binom.test(sum(tenx_deg$same_sign), nrow(tenx_deg), 0.5)$p.value else NA_real_,
    median_naive_over_clean_abs_log2FC = if (nrow(diluted) > 0)
      median(abs(diluted$naive_log2FC) / abs(diluted$gex_log2FC)) else NA_real_,
    p_naive_vs_clean_wilcoxon = if (nrow(diluted) > 1) tier_safe_p(
      wilcox.test(abs(diluted$naive_log2FC), abs(diluted$gex_log2FC),
                  paired = TRUE)$p.value) else NA_real_,
    n_CaRe_added_only_held_at_matched_n =
      sum(care_added$fraction_significant_matched_n >= 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_CaRe_added_only_in_TenX_untestable_cluster =
      sum(care_added$in_GEX_untestable_cluster),
    TenX_untestable_clusters = paste(untestable_clusters, collapse = ","),
    n_genes_significant_in_TenX_untestable_clusters = length(cluster_hits))
}

tier_concordance <- purrr::map_dfr(names(reference_contrasts), function(reference_contrast) {
  purrr::map_dfr(names(tiers_all), tier_concordance_one,
                 reference_contrast = reference_contrast)
})

cat("=== TenX reference vs Ca*Re-only DEG concordance (whole sample, matched negatives) ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(tier_concordance))
```

### Panel E: viral load as two groups

Also prints the in-text yield comparison: the Ca*Re positives of
`tier_binload_downsample` thinned to the number of cells its TenX arm calls, with
the same Wilcoxon re-run over `tier_binload_ndraw` draws

Writes `PanelE_loadState_binary_hallmark_lines.pdf`.
Prerequisites: the `pathway screen` chunk, for `<sample>_pathway_scores.csv`.
```{r tier_binary_load}
tier_binload.dir  <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/")
tier_binload_min  <- 10          # minimum cells in a load group before it is tested
tier_binload_out  <- paste0(plot.root, "Figure3/")
tier_binload_cut  <- 8
tier_binload_samples <- c("Invitro", "Pacute", "W2", "D195")
tier_binload_sets <- c("OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION", "GLYCOLYSIS", "MTORC1_SIGNALING",
                       "INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE", "TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB",
                       "INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE")
tier_binload_labels <- c(OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION = "OxPhos", GLYCOLYSIS = "Glycolysis",
                         MTORC1_SIGNALING = "mTORC1",
                         INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE = "IFN\u03b3",
                         TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB = "TNF\u03b1/NF\u03baB",
                         INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE = "Inflammatory")
# Facet strips are plotmath rather than the Unicode labels above: the figure is
# written on the default pdf device for Helvetica, and that device's Latin-1
# encoding carries no Greek. plotmath takes the Greek from the Symbol font.
tier_binload_plotmath <- c(OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION = '"OxPhos"',
                           GLYCOLYSIS = '"Glycolysis"',
                           MTORC1_SIGNALING = '"mTORC1"',
                           INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE = '"IFN"*gamma',
                           TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB = '"TNF"*alpha*"/NF"*kappa*"B"',
                           INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE = '"Inflammatory"')
tier_binload_pal <- c(Invitro = "#594A42", W2 = "#EE2A7B",
                      Pacute = "#DB73AD", D195 = "#A97C50")
# Samples are named for the condition they represent rather than the library, so
# the legend reads as the biology. Drawn in this order.
tier_binload_legend <- c(Invitro = "*in vitro*", W2 = "*in vivo* (W2)",
                         Pacute = "*in vivo* (Pacute)", D195 = "ART")
# The legend carries no key glyphs: each label is drawn in its series colour, so
# the colour is read off the word itself.
tier_binload_md <- function(s) {
  paste0("<span style='color:", tier_binload_pal[s], "'>", tier_binload_legend[s], "</span>")
}

tier_binload_scores <- bind_rows(lapply(tier_binload_samples, function(s) {
  f <- paste0(tier_binload.dir, s, "_pathway_scores.csv")
  if (!check_migrated(f)) return(NULL)
  read.csv(f) %>% mutate(sample = s)
})) %>%
  filter(tier %in% c("both", "CaRe_only", "neg")) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, tier_binload_samples),
         load = ifelse(tier == "neg", "uninfected",
                       ifelse(care_UMIs < tier_binload_cut,
                              paste0("2-", tier_binload_cut - 1),
                              paste0(tier_binload_cut, "+"))))

# Wilcoxon of each load group against that sample's uninfected cells, BH across
# the sample x set x group grid.
tier_binload_stats <- bind_rows(lapply(tier_binload_samples, function(s)
  bind_rows(lapply(intersect(tier_binload_sets, colnames(tier_binload_scores)), function(st) {
    q <- tier_binload_scores %>% filter(sample == s)
    ref <- q[[st]][q$load == "uninfected"]
    bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(unique(q$load), "uninfected"), function(gr) {
      x <- q[[st]][q$load == gr]
      if (length(x) < tier_binload_min) return(NULL)
      data.frame(sample = s, set = st, load = gr, n = length(x),
                 delta = mean(x) - mean(ref),
                 p = suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(x, ref)$p.value))
    }))
  })))) %>%
  mutate(padj = p.adjust(p, "BH"),
         set_expr = factor(tier_binload_plotmath[set],
                           levels = unname(tier_binload_plotmath)),
         set = factor(tier_binload_labels[set], levels = unname(tier_binload_labels)),
         load = factor(load, c(paste0("2-", tier_binload_cut - 1),
                               paste0(tier_binload_cut, "+"))),
         sample = factor(sample, tier_binload_samples))

cat("\n=== Hallmark module score by binary viral load, vs uninfected ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(tier_binload_stats %>%
  mutate(delta = round(delta, 3), padj = signif(padj, 2)) %>%
  select(sample, set, load, n, delta, padj) %>% arrange(set, sample, load)))

# --- In text: would 10X's cell yield have found the same shift? ---------------
# The TenX arm of `tier_binload_downsample` calls too few cells to test, and the
# ones it calls are GEX_only, a tier this chunk does not score, so they cannot be
# tested directly. The yield question is answered instead by thinning the Ca*Re
# positives to the TenX arm's cell count and re-running the identical Wilcoxon, so
# the only thing that changes between the two is how many cells the comparison
# has. Draws are taken before anything that reseeds the RNG.
tier_binload_downsample <- "D195"
tier_binload_ndraw      <- 2000
tier_binload_n_tenx <- sum(read.csv(paste0(tier_binload.dir, tier_binload_downsample,
                                          "_tiers.csv"))$tier %in% c("both", "GEX_only"))
tier_binload_q   <- tier_binload_scores %>% filter(sample == tier_binload_downsample)
tier_binload_pos <- tier_binload_q %>% filter(tier != "neg")
tier_binload_ref <- tier_binload_q %>% filter(tier == "neg")

# Every draw is tested against the same uninfected cells, so each positive
# cell's contribution to the Mann-Whitney U is counted once here and summed per
# draw, rather than calling wilcox.test for every draw x set. The module scores
# carry no ties, so wilcox.test takes the normal approximation with a continuity
# correction, which the p below reproduces exactly.
tier_binload_posm <- as.matrix(tier_binload_pos[, tier_binload_sets])
tier_binload_nref <- nrow(tier_binload_ref)
tier_binload_u <- vapply(tier_binload_sets, function(st) {
  reference <- sort(tier_binload_ref[[st]])
  below <- findInterval(tier_binload_posm[, st], reference, left.open = TRUE)
  below + 0.5 * (findInterval(tier_binload_posm[, st], reference) - below)
}, numeric(nrow(tier_binload_posm)))

tier_binload_bh <- function(rows) {
  n_pos  <- length(rows)
  u      <- colSums(tier_binload_u[rows, , drop = FALSE])
  centre <- n_pos * tier_binload_nref / 2
  spread <- sqrt(n_pos * tier_binload_nref * (n_pos + tier_binload_nref + 1) / 12)
  p.adjust(2 * pnorm(-abs((u - centre - sign(u - centre) * 0.5) / spread)), "BH")
}
tier_binload_full <- tier_binload_bh(seq_len(nrow(tier_binload_posm)))
set.seed(1)
tier_binload_draws <- t(vapply(
  replicate(tier_binload_ndraw,
            sample.int(nrow(tier_binload_posm), tier_binload_n_tenx), simplify = FALSE),
  tier_binload_bh, numeric(length(tier_binload_sets))))
colnames(tier_binload_draws) <- tier_binload_sets

cat("\n=== ", tier_binload_downsample, ": Ca*Re cells thinned to the TenX arm's yield (",
    tier_binload_n_tenx, " cells), ", tier_binload_ndraw, " draws ===\n", sep = "")
print(as.data.frame(tibble(
  set = unname(tier_binload_labels[tier_binload_sets]),
  full_arm_padj = signif(tier_binload_full, 2),
  median_padj   = signif(apply(tier_binload_draws, 2, median), 2),
  pct_draws_padj_lt_0.05 = round(100 * colMeans(tier_binload_draws < 0.05), 1))),
  row.names = FALSE)
cat("-> downsampling the Ca*Re-detected cells to the ", tier_binload_n_tenx,
    " cells 10X detected recovers the OxPhos shift in ",
    round(100 * mean(tier_binload_draws[, "OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION"] < 0.05), 1),
    "% of draws (full arm: n = ", nrow(tier_binload_pos), ", BH p = ",
    signif(tier_binload_full[["OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION"]], 2), ")\n", sep = "")

tier_binload_plot <- ggplot(tier_binload_stats,
                            aes(load, delta, color = sample, group = sample)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(size = ifelse(padj < 0.05, "padj<0.05", "ns"))) +
  facet_wrap(~ set_expr, nrow = 2, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_color_manual(values = tier_binload_pal, name = NULL,
                     breaks = names(tier_binload_legend),
                     labels = tier_binload_md(names(tier_binload_legend))) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c(`padj<0.05` = 3.4, ns = 1.4), name = NULL) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(order = 1,
                              override.aes = list(linewidth = 0, size = 0, stroke = 0)),
         size  = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  labs(x = "Ca*Re viral UMIs per cell", y = "module score vs uninfected") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1.05)),
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = rel(0.95)),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = rel(0.85),
                                               family = "Helvetica"),
        legend.key.spacing.x = unit(0.2, "cm"),
        legend.margin = margin(t = -4))
# The default pdf device, not cairo_pdf. Helvetica is one of the base-14 PDF
# fonts, so it is written by name instead of embedded, and Arial stands in for it
# on opening: the two share metrics, and no Arial is installed here for any
# device to use. cairo_pdf resolves the family through fontconfig, which holds
# neither, and would silently fall back to DejaVu Sans. The Greek in the facet
# strips survives because they are plotmath, drawn from the Symbol font.
ggsave(paste0(tier_binload_out, "PanelE_loadState_binary_hallmark_lines.pdf"),
       tier_binload_plot, width = 9, height = 6,
       device = grDevices::pdf, family = "Helvetica")
print(tier_binload_plot)
```

### Print: load vs pathway genes

Supports Fig 3E in-text statements

Prerequisites: the `tier_tables` chunk. Loads each per-sample Seurat RDS, so run
it on a compute node (srun, genomics partition).
```{r tier_load_genes}
loadgene_rds.dir   <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/singleCell/Seurat/RDS/")
loadgene_table.dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/")
loadgene_out.dir   <- paste0(loadgene_table.dir, "load_genes/")
dir.create(loadgene_out.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

loadgene_samples <- c("Invitro", "W2", "Pacute", "D195")
# The Panel C split, so the two analyses describe the same groups
loadgene_cut <- 8
loadgene_min_detected <- 0.05
loadgene_min_cells    <- 10
loadgene_fc    <- 0.5
loadgene_padj  <- 0.01
loadgene_n_random  <- 2000
loadgene_expr_bins <- 10
loadgene_sets <- c("OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION", "GLYCOLYSIS", "MTORC1_SIGNALING",
                   "INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE", "TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB",
                   "INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE")
loadgene_hallmark <- hallmark_gene_sets()
stopifnot(all(loadgene_sets %in% names(loadgene_hallmark)))

# Share of draws whose fraction_down reaches the set's, where a draw holds as
# many genes as the set does in each expression decile
loadgene_null_p <- function(log2FC, expression_bin, set_genes, seed = 1) {
  observed <- mean(log2FC[set_genes] < 0)
  wanted <- table(expression_bin[set_genes])
  pools  <- split(which(!set_genes), expression_bin[!set_genes])
  set.seed(seed)
  draws <- replicate(loadgene_n_random, {
    picked <- unlist(mapply(function(pool, n) pool[sample.int(length(pool), min(length(pool), n))],
                            pools[names(wanted)], wanted, SIMPLIFY = FALSE), use.names = FALSE)
    mean(log2FC[picked] < 0)
  })
  list(observed = observed, null_mean = mean(draws),
       p = (sum(draws >= observed) + 1) / (loadgene_n_random + 1))
}

loadgene_breadth <- list(); loadgene_core <- list()
for (sample_name in loadgene_samples) {
  seurat_file <- paste0(loadgene_rds.dir, sample_name, ".rds")
  tiers_file  <- paste0(loadgene_table.dir, sample_name, "_tiers.csv")
  if (!check_migrated(seurat_file) || !file.exists(tiers_file)) next
  tiers <- read.csv(tiers_file) %>% mutate(cellID = as.character(cellID)) %>%
    filter(tier %in% c("both", "CaRe_only", "neg"))
  obj <- readRDS(seurat_file)
  DefaultAssay(obj) <- "RNA"
  obj <- JoinLayers(obj, assay = "RNA")
  tiers <- tiers %>% filter(cellID %in% colnames(obj))
  obj <- subset(obj, cells = tiers$cellID)

  groups <- list(
    low  = tiers$cellID[tiers$tier != "neg" & tiers$care_UMIs <  loadgene_cut],
    high = tiers$cellID[tiers$tier != "neg" & tiers$care_UMIs >= loadgene_cut],
    uninfected = tiers$cellID[tiers$tier == "neg"])

  counts <- GetAssayData(obj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  universe <- names(which(Matrix::rowMeans(counts > 0) >= loadgene_min_detected))
  expression <- Matrix::rowMeans(GetAssayData(obj, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")[universe, ])
  expression_bin <- cut(expression, unique(quantile(expression,
                        seq(0, 1, length.out = loadgene_expr_bins + 1))), include.lowest = TRUE)
  cat("\n", sample_name, ": universe", length(universe), "genes | low",
      length(groups$low), "| high", length(groups$high), "| uninfected",
      length(groups$uninfected), "\n")

  contrasts <- list(low_vs_uninfected  = c("low", "uninfected"),
                    high_vs_uninfected = c("high", "uninfected"),
                    high_vs_low        = c("high", "low"))
  for (contrast_name in names(contrasts)) {
    pair <- contrasts[[contrast_name]]
    if (min(lengths(groups[pair])) < loadgene_min_cells) {
      cat("  skipping", contrast_name, "- fewer than", loadgene_min_cells, "cells\n"); next
    }
    deg <- FindMarkers(obj, ident.1 = groups[[pair[1]]], ident.2 = groups[[pair[2]]],
                       features = universe, assay = "RNA", test.use = "wilcox",
                       logfc.threshold = 0, min.pct = 0, verbose = FALSE)
    deg$gene <- rownames(deg)
    write.csv(deg, paste0(loadgene_out.dir, sample_name, "_load_", contrast_name,
                          "_genes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    log2FC <- setNames(deg$avg_log2FC, deg$gene)[universe]
    padj   <- setNames(deg$p_val_adj,  deg$gene)[universe]

    for (set_name in loadgene_sets) {
      set_genes <- universe %in% loadgene_hallmark[[set_name]]
      if (sum(set_genes) < 10) next
      null <- loadgene_null_p(log2FC, expression_bin, set_genes)
      loadgene_breadth[[length(loadgene_breadth) + 1]] <- tibble(
        sample = sample_name, contrast = contrast_name, set = set_name,
        n_genes = sum(set_genes),
        fraction_down = round(null$observed, 3),
        fraction_down_null = round(null$null_mean, 3),
        mean_log2FC = round(mean(log2FC[set_genes]), 4),
        mean_pct_per_gene = round(100 * (2^mean(log2FC[set_genes]) - 1), 2),
        p_empirical = null$p)
      core <- which(set_genes & padj < loadgene_padj & abs(log2FC) > loadgene_fc)
      loadgene_core[[length(loadgene_core) + 1]] <- tibble(
        sample = sample_name, contrast = contrast_name, set = set_name,
        n_core = length(core),
        genes = paste(universe[core][order(-abs(log2FC[core]))], collapse = ";"))
    }
  }
  rm(obj, counts); gc()
}

loadgene_breadth <- bind_rows(loadgene_breadth) %>%
  mutate(p_adj = signif(p.adjust(p_empirical, "BH"), 2))
loadgene_core <- bind_rows(loadgene_core)
write.csv(loadgene_breadth, paste0(loadgene_out.dir, "load_gene_breadth.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(loadgene_core,    paste0(loadgene_out.dir, "load_gene_core.csv"),    row.names = FALSE)

# The full grids stay in the two CSVs above; what prints is only the three
# quantities the Fig 3E text quotes.

cat("\n=== 1. Oxidative phosphorylation: share of genes down vs uninfected ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(loadgene_breadth %>%
  filter(set == "OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION", contrast != "high_vs_low") %>%
  transmute(load = sub("_vs_uninfected", "", contrast), sample, n_genes,
            pct_down      = round(100 * fraction_down),
            pct_down_null = round(100 * fraction_down_null),
            pct_per_gene  = mean_pct_per_gene, p_adj) %>%
  arrange(load, sample)), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== 2. Other sets reduced at low load (FDR < 0.05, above the null) ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(loadgene_breadth %>%
  filter(set != "OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION", contrast == "low_vs_uninfected",
         p_adj < 0.05, fraction_down > fraction_down_null) %>%
  transmute(set, sample, n_genes,
            pct_down      = round(100 * fraction_down),
            pct_down_null = round(100 * fraction_down_null), p_adj) %>%
  arrange(set, sample)), row.names = FALSE)

# The text's core set is the genes that pass the DEG call against uninfected
# cells AND against the low-load cells, so a gene called against only one of the
# two references does not count.
loadgene_inflammatory <- c("TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB", "INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE")
loadgene_high_core <- loadgene_core %>%
  filter(set %in% loadgene_inflammatory, n_core > 0,
         contrast %in% c("high_vs_uninfected", "high_vs_low")) %>%
  mutate(gene = strsplit(genes, ";")) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(gene) %>%
  group_by(sample, gene) %>%
  summarize(n_contrasts = n_distinct(contrast), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_contrasts == 2)

cat("\n=== 3. High-load core: inflammatory and TNFA genes passing against both",
    "low load and uninfected ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(
  tibble(sample = intersect(loadgene_samples, unique(loadgene_core$sample))) %>%
    left_join(loadgene_high_core %>% group_by(sample) %>%
                summarize(n_core = n(), genes = paste(sort(gene), collapse = ", "),
                          .groups = "drop"),
              by = "sample") %>%
    mutate(n_core = coalesce(n_core, 0L), genes = coalesce(genes, "(none)"))),
  row.names = FALSE)
```


### cNMF programs
Pattern usage per tier on the cleaned cNMF runs of Panels E and F: TenX-positive
vs uninfected, both vs uninfected and Ca*Re-only vs uninfected, each by
`compare_pattern_usage` (Wilcoxon, BH across the patterns of a contrast). The two
single-chemistry contrasts are also drawn as a supplemental barplot,
`cNMF_tier_program_enrichment.pdf`, which asks what the cells each chemistry
calls contribute in program space.

Ca*Re-only vs TenX-positive is not among the contrasts. Those two groups differ
mainly in viral burden, so the comparison restates the Panel C load contrast,
which tests it directly and on a cut point set from the burden distribution.

Host library size is neither regressed out nor matched on here: the gap in it
between infected and uninfected cells is a property of infected cells rather than
a detection artifact, so removing it would take real signal with it
(SuppFigs.Rmd, `suppfig3_depth_confounding`).
Negatives are all `neg` CD4 T cells in the cNMF run, unmatched.
Prerequisites: the `tier_tables` chunk and the cleaned cNMF usage tables.
```{r tier_cnmf}
table.dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/")
supp.dir  <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig3/")
dir.create(supp.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

tenx_positive_tiers <- c("both", "GEX_only")
tier_cnmf_samples  <- c("Invitro", "W2", "Pacute")
tiers_all <- read_tier_tables(table.dir, tier_cnmf_samples)

# The two contrasts the supplemental barplot draws, in plotting order
tier_cnmf_panel_contrasts <- c("TenX-positive vs uninfected",
                               "Ca*Re-only vs uninfected")
tier_cnmf_colors <- c(`GEX-positive vs uninfected` = "#2B3990",
                      `Ca*Re-only vs uninfected`   = "#00AEEF")
# Each contrast is run against every uninfected cell and against uninfected
# cells matched on host library size decile, drawn as the two rows of the panel
tier_cnmf_references <- c("all uninfected cells", "host size decile matched")
tier_cnmf_call_padj  <- 0.05

# `prefix` is the tag the joint run puts on its cell IDs, stripped to recover the
# barcode the tier tables carry.
integrated_usage <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                           "combined/cNMF/subpattern/Pacute_W2_integrated_usage_K6.csv")
tier_cnmf <- list(
  Invitro = list(usage_file = paste0(data.root,
                                     "Figure1/singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/",
                                     "Invitro_cleaned_usage_K5.csv"),
                 prefix = NULL, labels = cnmf_metaprogram_labels$Invitro),
  W2      = list(usage_file = integrated_usage, prefix = "W2_",
                 labels = cnmf_integrated_metaprogram_labels),
  Pacute  = list(usage_file = integrated_usage, prefix = "Pacute_",
                 labels = cnmf_integrated_metaprogram_labels))

tier_cnmf_enrichment <- purrr::map_dfr(tier_cnmf_samples, function(sample_name) {
  cfg <- tier_cnmf[[sample_name]]
  if (!check_migrated(cfg$usage_file)) return(NULL)
  usage <- read.csv(cfg$usage_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(cfg$prefix)) {
    usage <- usage[grepl(paste0("^", cfg$prefix), rownames(usage)), , drop = FALSE]
    rownames(usage) <- sub(paste0("^", cfg$prefix), "", rownames(usage))
  }
  tiers <- tiers_all[[sample_name]] %>% filter(cellID %in% rownames(usage))
  host_size <- setNames(tiers$size, tiers$cellID)

  tenx_positive <- tiers$cellID[tiers$tier %in% tenx_positive_tiers]
  called_both  <- tiers$cellID[tiers$tier == "both"]
  care_only    <- tiers$cellID[tiers$tier == "CaRe_only"]
  negative     <- tiers$cellID[tiers$tier == "neg"]

  tier_pairs <- list(
    list(label = "TenX-positive vs uninfected", cells = list(tenx_positive, negative),
         labels = c("TenX_positive", "neg")),
    list(label = "both vs uninfected",         cells = list(called_both, negative),
         labels = c("both", "neg")),
    list(label = "Ca*Re-only vs uninfected",   cells = list(care_only, negative),
         labels = c("CaRe_only", "neg")))

  purrr::map_dfr(tier_pairs, function(pair) {
    if (min(lengths(pair$cells)) < 3) {
      cat("Skipping", sample_name, pair$label, "- fewer than 3 cells\n")
      return(NULL)
    }
    comparisons <- list(
      compare_pattern_usage(usage, pair$cells[[1]], pair$cells[[2]],
                            group_labels = pair$labels),
      compare_pattern_usage_matched(usage, pair$cells[[1]], pair$cells[[2]],
                                    match_values = host_size,
                                    group_labels = pair$labels))
    purrr::map2_dfr(comparisons, tier_cnmf_references, function(comparison, reference) {
      result <- merge(comparison$comparison,
                      comparison$stats[, c("pattern", "p_adj")], by = "pattern")
      cat("\n", sample_name, pair$label, "|", reference, "(",
          nrow(comparison$group1_patterns), "vs",
          nrow(comparison$group2_patterns), "cells )\n")
      print(result)
      result %>%
        transmute(sample = sample_name, contrast = pair$label, reference, pattern,
                  program = cfg$labels[pattern],
                  n_positive  = nrow(comparison$group1_patterns),
                  n_reference = nrow(comparison$group2_patterns),
                  log2_fold_change, p_adj)
    })
  })
})

# Programs are ordered by metaprogram number, which is shared across the runs, so
# every facet reads left to right on the same axis.
tier_cnmf_plot_data <- tier_cnmf_enrichment %>%
  filter(contrast %in% tier_cnmf_panel_contrasts,
         !grepl("contaminant|contamination", program, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(sample      = factor(sample, levels = tier_cnmf_samples),
         contrast    = factor(contrast, levels = tier_cnmf_panel_contrasts),
         reference   = factor(reference, levels = tier_cnmf_references),
         significant = p_adj < tier_cnmf_call_padj,
         label_y     = log2_fold_change + sign(log2_fold_change) * 0.07)
tier_cnmf_plot_data$program <- factor(
  tier_cnmf_plot_data$program,
  levels = unique(tier_cnmf_plot_data$program[
    order(as.numeric(sub("^M([0-9]+).*", "\\1", tier_cnmf_plot_data$program)))]))

tier_cnmf_panel <- ggplot(tier_cnmf_plot_data,
                          aes(program, log2_fold_change, fill = contrast)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(y = label_y, label = ifelse(significant, "*", "ns")),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 2.4, vjust = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(reference ~ sample, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tier_cnmf_colors, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "log2 fold change in mean program usage",
       caption = paste0("Wilcoxon, BH across the patterns of a contrast; * padj < ",
                        tier_cnmf_call_padj,
                        ". Pacute and W2 share one joint cNMF run; Invitro has its own.")) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom")

ggsave(paste0(supp.dir, "cNMF_tier_program_enrichment.pdf"),
       tier_cnmf_panel, width = 11, height = 7)
print(tier_cnmf_panel)

cat("\n=== Programs moved per contrast (padj <", tier_cnmf_call_padj, ") ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(tier_cnmf_plot_data %>%
  group_by(sample, reference, contrast) %>%
  summarize(n_programs = n(), n_significant = sum(significant),
            max_abs_log2FC = round(max(abs(log2_fold_change)), 2),
            .groups = "drop")), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== M1 resting/memory, the contrast the two chemistries disagree on ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(tier_cnmf_plot_data %>%
  filter(grepl("^M1 ", program)) %>%
  transmute(sample, reference, contrast, n_positive,
            log2_fold_change = round(log2_fold_change, 3),
            p_adj = signif(p_adj, 2)) %>%
  arrange(sample, reference, contrast)), row.names = FALSE)
```


### Program usage across the viral load range and by infected-population definition
What every cNMF program does across the viral load spectrum, which the Panel E
load-state analysis asks of the Hallmark sets. Three framings, because the answer
depends on which infected cells an assay samples:

  - five load bins, which show the shape of the gradient
  - four definitions of the infected population: every Ca*Re-called cell, the
    low and high halves of the 8 UMI split, and the cells the 10X arm calls.
    Methods that isolate infected cells on proviral DNA mix silent, low- and
    high-transcribing cells, so the pooled Ca*Re arm rather than either half is
    the comparable population.
  - Spearman of usage against load among virus-transcribing cells, and a
    bootstrap confidence interval on each population's log2 fold change, so that
    a difference which does not reach significance is reported as a bounded
    interval rather than as an absence

W2 and Pacute read from the joint cNMF run, which puts them on identical
programs; Invitro and D195 have their own runs. Contaminant programs carry no
claim about infected-cell state and are dropped.

Writes `SuppFig3_cnmf_loadBins.csv`, `SuppFig3_cnmf_populations.csv`,
`SuppFig3_cnmf_loadCorrelation.csv` and `SuppFig3_cnmf_bootstrapCI.csv`.
Prerequisites: the `tier_tables` chunk and the cleaned cNMF usage tables. Reads
those tables only, so it does not need a compute node.
```{r suppfig3_cnmf_load_populations}
cnmfload_table.dir  <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/")
cnmfload_output.dir <- paste0(plot.root, "Supplemental/SuppFig3/")
dir.create(cnmfload_output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

cnmfload_samples    <- c("Invitro", "W2", "Pacute", "D195")
# The Panel C/E split, so this analysis describes the same load groups
cnmfload_cut        <- 8
cnmfload_breaks     <- c(0, 3, 7, 15, 31, Inf)
cnmfload_bin_labels <- c("2-3", "4-7", "8-15", "16-31", "32+")
cnmfload_min_cells  <- 10
cnmfload_n_boot     <- 10000
cnmfload_population_levels <- c("all Ca*Re", "low (2-7)", "high (8+)", "10X-called")

cnmfload_integrated <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                              "combined/cNMF/subpattern/Pacute_W2_integrated_usage_K6.csv")
cnmfload_usage <- list(
  Invitro = list(file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                               "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/Invitro_cleaned_usage_K5.csv"),
                 prefix = NULL, labels = cnmf_metaprogram_labels$Invitro),
  W2      = list(file = cnmfload_integrated, prefix = "W2_",
                 labels = cnmf_integrated_metaprogram_labels),
  Pacute  = list(file = cnmfload_integrated, prefix = "Pacute_",
                 labels = cnmf_integrated_metaprogram_labels),
  D195    = list(file = paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                               "singleCell/cNMF/subpattern/D195_cleaned_usage_K6.csv"),
                 prefix = NULL, labels = cnmf_metaprogram_labels$D195))

cnmfload_tiers <- read_tier_tables(cnmfload_table.dir, cnmfload_samples)

# Usage table for one sample, with the joint run's cell ID tag stripped
cnmfload_read <- function(cfg) {
  if (!file.exists(cfg$file)) return(NULL)
  usage <- read.csv(cfg$file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(cfg$prefix)) {
    usage <- usage[grepl(paste0("^", cfg$prefix), rownames(usage)), , drop = FALSE]
    rownames(usage) <- sub(paste0("^", cfg$prefix), "", rownames(usage))
  }
  usage
}

cnmfload_cells <- purrr::map_dfr(cnmfload_samples, function(sample_name) {
  cfg <- cnmfload_usage[[sample_name]]
  usage <- cnmfload_read(cfg)
  if (is.null(usage)) { cat("missing usage table:", sample_name, "\n"); return(NULL) }
  tiers <- cnmfload_tiers[[sample_name]] %>%
    filter(tier %in% c("both", "CaRe_only", "GEX_only", "neg"),
           cellID %in% rownames(usage))
  as_tibble(usage[tiers$cellID, , drop = FALSE]) %>%
    mutate(sample = sample_name, cellID = tiers$cellID, tier = tiers$tier,
           care_UMIs = tiers$care_UMIs, GEX_UMIs = tiers$GEX_UMIs) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(starts_with("Pattern_"), names_to = "pattern", values_to = "usage") %>%
    mutate(program = cfg$labels[pattern])
}) %>%
  filter(!is.na(program),
         !grepl("contaminant|contamination", program, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, cnmfload_samples),
         load_bin = cut(care_UMIs, cnmfload_breaks, labels = cnmfload_bin_labels))

# Cells of one infected-population definition
cnmfload_population <- function(cells, population) {
  switch(population,
    `all Ca*Re`  = cells %>% filter(tier != "neg", care_UMIs > 0),
    `low (2-7)`  = cells %>% filter(tier != "neg", care_UMIs > 0, care_UMIs < cnmfload_cut),
    `high (8+)`  = cells %>% filter(tier != "neg", care_UMIs >= cnmfload_cut),
    `10X-called` = cells %>% filter(tier != "neg", GEX_UMIs > 0))
}

cnmfload_log2FC <- function(tested, reference) {
  log2((mean(tested) + 1e-10) / (mean(reference) + 1e-10))
}

# Usage by load bin, against the sample's uninfected cells
cnmfload_bins <- purrr::map_dfr(levels(cnmfload_cells$sample), function(sample_name) {
  sample_cells <- cnmfload_cells %>% filter(sample == sample_name)
  purrr::map_dfr(unique(sample_cells$program), function(program_name) {
    program_cells <- sample_cells %>% filter(program == program_name)
    reference <- program_cells %>% filter(tier == "neg")
    if (nrow(reference) < cnmfload_min_cells) return(NULL)
    purrr::map_dfr(cnmfload_bin_labels, function(bin) {
      tested <- program_cells %>% filter(tier != "neg", care_UMIs > 0, load_bin == bin)
      if (nrow(tested) < cnmfload_min_cells) return(NULL)
      tibble(sample = sample_name, program = program_name, load_bin = bin,
             n_cells = nrow(tested),
             log2FC = cnmfload_log2FC(tested$usage, reference$usage),
             p_value = tier_safe_p(wilcox.test(tested$usage, reference$usage)$p.value))
    })
  })
}) %>% group_by(sample) %>% mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, "BH")) %>% ungroup()

# Usage by infected-population definition, with a bootstrap CI on each log2FC
cnmfload_populations <- purrr::map_dfr(levels(cnmfload_cells$sample), function(sample_name) {
  sample_cells <- cnmfload_cells %>% filter(sample == sample_name)
  purrr::map_dfr(unique(sample_cells$program), function(program_name) {
    program_cells <- sample_cells %>% filter(program == program_name)
    reference <- program_cells %>% filter(tier == "neg")
    if (nrow(reference) < cnmfload_min_cells) return(NULL)
    purrr::map_dfr(cnmfload_population_levels, function(population) {
      tested <- cnmfload_population(program_cells, population)
      if (nrow(tested) < cnmfload_min_cells) return(NULL)
      set.seed(1)
      draws <- replicate(cnmfload_n_boot, {
        cnmfload_log2FC(sample(tested$usage, nrow(tested), TRUE),
                        sample(reference$usage, nrow(reference), TRUE))
      })
      ci <- quantile(draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
      tibble(sample = sample_name, program = program_name, population = population,
             n_cells = nrow(tested), n_reference = nrow(reference),
             log2FC = cnmfload_log2FC(tested$usage, reference$usage),
             ci_low = ci[[1]], ci_high = ci[[2]],
             p_value = tier_safe_p(wilcox.test(tested$usage, reference$usage)$p.value))
    })
  })
}) %>% group_by(sample) %>% mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, "BH")) %>% ungroup()

# Spearman of usage against load, among virus-transcribing cells only
cnmfload_correlation <- cnmfload_cells %>%
  filter(tier != "neg", care_UMIs > 0) %>%
  group_by(sample, program) %>%
  filter(n() >= cnmfload_min_cells) %>%
  summarize(n_cells = n(),
            rho = tier_safe_p(cor(usage, care_UMIs, method = "spearman")),
            p_value = tier_safe_p(cor.test(usage, care_UMIs, method = "spearman")$p.value),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(sample) %>% mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, "BH")) %>% ungroup()

write.csv(cnmfload_bins, paste0(cnmfload_output.dir, "SuppFig3_cnmf_loadBins.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(cnmfload_populations %>% select(-ci_low, -ci_high),
          paste0(cnmfload_output.dir, "SuppFig3_cnmf_populations.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(cnmfload_populations %>%
            select(sample, program, population, n_cells, log2FC, ci_low, ci_high, p_adj),
          paste0(cnmfload_output.dir, "SuppFig3_cnmf_bootstrapCI.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(cnmfload_correlation,
          paste0(cnmfload_output.dir, "SuppFig3_cnmf_loadCorrelation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== Program usage by load bin, log2FC vs uninfected ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(cnmfload_bins %>%
  transmute(sample, program, load_bin, n_cells, log2FC = round(log2FC, 3),
            p_adj = signif(p_adj, 2)) %>%
  arrange(sample, program, factor(load_bin, cnmfload_bin_labels))), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== Program usage by infected-population definition, with bootstrap CI ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(cnmfload_populations %>%
  transmute(sample, program, population, n_cells, log2FC = round(log2FC, 3),
            CI = paste0("[", round(ci_low, 3), ", ", round(ci_high, 3), "]"),
            p_adj = signif(p_adj, 2)) %>%
  arrange(sample, program, factor(population, cnmfload_population_levels))), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== Spearman: program usage against load among infected cells ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(cnmfload_correlation %>%
  transmute(sample, program, n_cells, rho = round(rho, 3), p_adj = signif(p_adj, 2)) %>%
  arrange(sample, program)), row.names = FALSE)
```


### Supp Fig 3 Panel B: host library size control
Made in SuppFigs.Rmd (`suppfig3_panelB_hostsize`), from the tier tables and
the cleaned cNMF usage tables the chunk above reads.


### Published marker panels and per-gene tests on the infected populations
Whether the published descriptions of infected and reservoir cells hold on each
infected-population definition, tested as marker panels rather than as cNMF
programs so the comparison does not depend on our own factorization. Each panel
is named for the study whose claim it tests, and each is scored with
`AddModuleScore` and compared against `n_random` expression-matched random gene
sets, since infected cells carry more host RNA and a random set of the same size
and expression profile therefore also shifts away from zero. The individual
marker genes are tested on their own as well, because a panel can be null while
single genes within it move.

This loads each per-sample Seurat RDS, so it does not run in the knit. Run
`extractionScripts/submissionScripts/Figure3/suppfig3_marker_panels.sh` on a compute node first; it writes
`SuppFig3_markerPanels_null.csv` and `SuppFig3_markerPanels_perGene.csv`, which
this chunk reads.

Prerequisites: the `tier_tables` chunk, and `extractionScripts/submissionScripts/Figure3/suppfig3_marker_panels.sh`
already run.
```{r suppfig3_marker_panels}
markerpanel_output.dir <- cnmfload_output.dir
markerpanel_null_file   <- paste0(markerpanel_output.dir, "SuppFig3_markerPanels_null.csv")
markerpanel_gene_file   <- paste0(markerpanel_output.dir, "SuppFig3_markerPanels_perGene.csv")
markerpanel_populations <- c("all Ca*Re", "low (2-7)", "high (8+)", "10X-called")
# The genes the Supplementary text quotes, drawn out of the full per-gene table
markerpanel_genes <- c("BACH2", "SATB1", "CD28", "IL21R", "CD44", "IL7R", "CCR7", "TCF7")

if (!file.exists(markerpanel_null_file) || !file.exists(markerpanel_gene_file)) {
  cat("Run extractionScripts/submissionScripts/Figure3/suppfig3_marker_panels.sh first; expected\n  ",
      markerpanel_null_file, "\n  ", markerpanel_gene_file, "\n")
} else {
  markerpanel_null <- read.csv(markerpanel_null_file, check.names = FALSE)
  markerpanel_gene <- read.csv(markerpanel_gene_file, check.names = FALSE)

  cat("\n=== Marker panels against an expression-matched random-gene null ===\n")
  print(as.data.frame(markerpanel_null %>%
    transmute(sample, population = arm, set, n_cells, n_genes,
              observed = round(observed, 4), null_mean = round(null_mean, 4),
              z = round(z, 2), p_two_sided = signif(p_two_sided, 2)) %>%
    arrange(sample, set, factor(population, markerpanel_populations))), row.names = FALSE)

  cat("\n=== Marker genes quoted in the text, per population ===\n")
  print(as.data.frame(markerpanel_gene %>%
    filter(gene %in% markerpanel_genes) %>%
    transmute(sample, gene, population = arm, log2FC = round(log2FC, 3),
              pct_population = round(pct_arm, 1), pct_uninfected = round(pct_neg, 1),
              p_adj = signif(p_adj, 2)) %>%
    arrange(gene, sample, factor(population, markerpanel_populations))), row.names = FALSE)
}
```



### Panel I: host state of splice+ vs splice- cells on ART
Whether the D195 cells carrying a spliced viral UMI sit anywhere different in
host transcriptome space from the ones that do not. A cell is virus-transcribing
if either chemistry calls it, and splice+ if either arm sees a spliced UMI, which
is the same definition Panels G and H use (`total > 0` on the combined table) and
the one the Invitro and W2 panels use, so the three samples are counted alike.
That gives 19 splice+ and 23 splice-; the 3 cells only the TenX arm calls were
assayed for splicing and carry none, so they are splice-, not missing data.

Two separation statistics, each against `hoststate_nperm` permutations of the
splice labels among the same cells. The null is what makes a negative result
interpretable: at these group sizes any two groups sit some distance apart, and
the null says how far apart label noise alone puts them. Statistics are computed
on the leading `REDUCTION_DIMENSIONS` principal components.

  - `pseudo_F`    PERMANOVA (Anderson 2001) on the Euclidean distances,
    between-group over within-group sum of squares, via `vegan::adonis2`.
  - `silhouette`  mean silhouette width of the splice labelling
    (`cluster::silhouette`): ~0 means a cell is no closer to its own group than
    to the other.

Both are one-sided upper: only "further apart than chance" is evidence of a
difference. `adonis2` runs its own permutations, so its p comes from the same
procedure as the silhouette null rather than from a distributional assumption.

A null here can be multimodal when a few cells lie far from the rest, since a
shuffle either splits them between the groups or does not. The chunk therefore
repeats both tests on the cells surviving a label-blind outlier screen, and
prints that, so the legend can say whether the result rests on those cells.

Prerequisites: the `tier_tables` chunk has written `D195_tiers.csv`, and
`D195.rds` exists. Loads that object for its PCA, so run on a compute node.
Needs `vegan` and `cluster`.
```{r d195_splice_hoststate}
hoststate.dir   <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/")
hoststate_rds   <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/singleCell/Seurat/RDS/D195.rds")
output.dir      <- paste0(plot.root, "Figure3/")
dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
hoststate_nperm <- 5000

hoststate_cells <- read.csv(paste0(hoststate.dir, "tiers/D195_tiers.csv")) %>%
  mutate(cellID = as.character(cellID)) %>%
  filter(care_UMIs > 0 | GEX_UMIs > 0) %>%
  mutate(splice = ifelse(care_spliced | GEX_spliced, "splice+", "splice-"))

hoststate_obj <- readRDS(hoststate_rds)
hoststate_emb <- Embeddings(hoststate_obj, reduction = "pca")[, 1:REDUCTION_DIMENSIONS, drop = FALSE]
rm(hoststate_obj); gc()
hoststate_cells <- hoststate_cells %>% filter(cellID %in% rownames(hoststate_emb))
hoststate_emb <- hoststate_emb[hoststate_cells$cellID, , drop = FALSE]
hoststate_labels <- hoststate_cells$splice

# Both statistics take their data explicitly rather than closing over the
# embedding, so the outlier rerun below cannot silently test the wrong matrix.
hoststate_silhouette <- function(labels, D) {
  mean(cluster::silhouette(as.integer(factor(labels)), dmatrix = D)[, "sil_width"])
}
hoststate_adonis <- function(labels, D) {
  unname(vegan::adonis2(D ~ labels, permutations = hoststate_nperm)$F[1])
}

# Permutations are drawn before anything that might seed the RNG itself (Seurat's
# FindMarkers takes `random.seed` and does), so the null cannot silently collapse
# to one shuffle repeated nperm times. The stopifnot fails loudly if it does.
hoststate_test <- function(emb, labels, tag) {
  D <- dist(emb)
  Dm <- as.matrix(D)
  set.seed(1)
  perms <- replicate(hoststate_nperm, sample(labels), simplify = FALSE)
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(perms, paste, character(1), collapse = ""))) >
              hoststate_nperm / 2)

  # adonis2 permutes internally and returns its own p; the silhouette null is
  # built from the same shuffles used for every other permutation test here.
  fit <- vegan::adonis2(D ~ labels, permutations = hoststate_nperm)
  # adonis2 keeps its permuted F values, so the panel can draw the same null the
  # p-value came from instead of a second one built here.
  f_null <- as.numeric(vegan::permustats(fit)$permutations)
  sil_observed <- hoststate_silhouette(labels, Dm)
  sil_null <- vapply(perms, hoststate_silhouette, numeric(1), D = Dm)

  list(
    null = bind_rows(tibble(statistic = "pseudo_F", value = f_null),
                     tibble(statistic = "silhouette", value = sil_null)),
    result = bind_rows(
      tibble(analysis = tag, statistic = "pseudo_F", n_cells = length(labels),
             observed = unname(fit$F[1]), null_mean = mean(f_null),
             p_perm = unname(fit$`Pr(>F)`[1])),
      tibble(analysis = tag, statistic = "silhouette", n_cells = length(labels),
             observed = sil_observed, null_mean = mean(sil_null),
             p_perm = (sum(sil_null >= sil_observed) + 1) / (hoststate_nperm + 1))))
}

hoststate_main <- hoststate_test(hoststate_emb, hoststate_labels, "all cells")

# Outliers are chosen by distance to the overall centroid, without reference to
# the splice labels, so the screen cannot create or erase a group difference.
hoststate_mad_cut <- 5
hoststate_d_centre <- sqrt(rowSums(sweep(hoststate_emb, 2, colMeans(hoststate_emb))^2))
hoststate_keep <- hoststate_d_centre <=
  median(hoststate_d_centre) + hoststate_mad_cut * mad(hoststate_d_centre)
hoststate_result <- if (all(hoststate_keep)) hoststate_main$result else
  bind_rows(hoststate_main$result,
            hoststate_test(hoststate_emb[hoststate_keep, , drop = FALSE],
                           hoststate_labels[hoststate_keep],
                           paste0("outliers dropped (n=", sum(hoststate_keep), ")"))$result)

cat("=== D195 splice+ vs splice-: separation in PC space,",
    hoststate_nperm, "permutations ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(hoststate_result %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3)))),
      row.names = FALSE)
cat("cells:", nrow(hoststate_emb), "| splice+:", sum(hoststate_labels == "splice+"),
    "| PCs:", ncol(hoststate_emb),
    "| outliers dropped:", sum(!hoststate_keep),
    if (any(!hoststate_keep)) paste0(" (", paste(hoststate_labels[!hoststate_keep],
                                                 collapse = ", "), ")") else "", "\n")

hoststate_labels_pretty <- c(pseudo_F = "PERMANOVA pseudo-F", silhouette = "mean silhouette width")
hoststate_null_df <- hoststate_main$null %>%
  mutate(statistic = hoststate_labels_pretty[statistic])
hoststate_observed_df <- hoststate_main$result %>%
  mutate(statistic = hoststate_labels_pretty[statistic])
hoststate_null_plot <- ggplot(hoststate_null_df, aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "grey78", color = NA) +
  geom_vline(data = hoststate_observed_df, aes(xintercept = observed),
             color = "#54278F", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = hoststate_observed_df, aes(x = observed, y = Inf,
                                              label = paste0("p = ", signif(p_perm, 2))),
            hjust = -0.15, vjust = 1.6, size = 2.5, color = "#54278F") +
  facet_wrap(~ statistic, scales = "free", nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = paste0("permutations (of ", hoststate_nperm, ")"),
       subtitle = "purple = observed splice labels; grey = permuted labels") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.3))

ggsave(paste0(output.dir, "PanelI_D195_splice_hostState.pdf"),
       hoststate_null_plot, width = 6, height = 2.6)
write.csv(hoststate_result, paste0(output.dir, "PanelI_D195_splice_hostState.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```


# Public data
This section applies the above Figure3 analysis to two public human datasets:
Collora et al. 2022 is unstimulated CD4+ T cells,  2nd letter V = viremic,
S = suppressed (ART), and 2023Rep* are uninfected controls.
HIV-seq is Frouard et al. 2026: week0 = pre-ART/viremic, week24/week45 = 
on-ART/suppressed, using only the "Primer" (HIV-enriched) libraries. 
Both went through the same joint GRCh38+HXB2 cellranger alignment (stepOne) and
bamsort (stepTwo).

Note six PID8027 fastq from GEO GSE266455 incorrect labels were reassigned:
week0replicate1NOTHING <-> week45replicate4NOTHING, week0replicate2NOTHING <->
week0replicate5Primer, week0replicate6Primer <-> week45replicate3NOTHING.
Our correction was post-hoc so cellranger's `web_summary.html`, the BAM `@RG` 
tag are still the incorrect original sample IDs.

## Load
Prerequisite: the Integrate chunk below has been run once for that
pass, so the `<condition>_<participant>.rds` files exist. Rerun after changing
`min_hiv_reads`, a dataset's `hiv_rule`, `hiv_tcell_gate` or `public_pass`

```{r public_load}
# --- settings ---------------------------------------------------------------
min_hiv_reads  <- 2       # HXB2 reads per barcode
hiv_tcell_gate <- TRUE    # CD4 T by ADT protein, by gene where there is no ADT
public_pass    <- "Viremic"     # or c("ART", "Uninfected")
public_load_datasets <- c("HIVseq", "Collora")
options(future.globals.maxSize = 8 * 1024^3)  # 8 GiB

# --- datasets ---------------------------------------------------------------
public_datasets <- list(
  Collora = list(
    results    = "collora_res",

  HIVseq = list(
    results    = "hivseq_res",
    deg.dir    = paste0(data.root, "HIVseq/DEG/"),
    conditions = c("Viremic", "ART"))
)

public_paths <- list(
  Collora = list(

    bamsort    = paste0(data.root, "Collora/bamsort"),

                      max_counts = Inf, max_mito = 10),
```
