```{r public_load}
  HIVseq = list(
    counts     = paste0(public.root, "HIVseq/counts"),
    bamsort    = paste0(data.root, "HIVseq/bamsort"),
    rds        = paste0(data.root, "HIVseq/Seurat/RDS_publishedQC"),
    integrated = paste0(data.root, "HIVseq/Seurat/integrated_publishedQC"),
    qc         = list(min_features = 500, max_features = Inf,
                      max_counts = Inf, max_mito = 15))
)

# --- sample maps ------------------------------------------------------------
collora_conditions <- tibble::tribble(
  ~sample,    ~condition,
  "DV739","Viremic", "DV799","Viremic", "DV910","Viremic",
  "IV236","Viremic", "IV640","Viremic", "IV829","Viremic",
  "RIV236","Viremic","RIV829","Viremic",
  "DS739","ART", "DS799","ART", "DS910","ART",

  "2023Rep1","Uninfected", "2023Rep2","Uninfected"
) %>%
  mutate(participant = sub("^[A-Za-z]+", "", sample))

hivseq_samples <- sub("_bamsort_alignment_LTR_D1.csv$", "", basename(
  Sys.glob(file.path(public_paths$HIVseq$bamsort,
                     "*_bamsort_alignment_LTR_D1.csv"))))
hivseq_samples <- hivseq_samples[grepl("Primer$", hivseq_samples)]
hivseq_conditions <- tibble(sample = hivseq_samples) %>%
  mutate(condition   = ifelse(grepl("week0", sample), "Viremic", "ART"),
         participant = sub("PID(\\d+).*", "\\1", sample))

public_maps <- list(Collora = collora_conditions, HIVseq = hivseq_conditions)

# --- reload -----------------------------------------------------------------
# A dataset with no cached integration for this pass warns and is skipped
```

## Extraction
Run these chunks in order

### Per-sample objects
Prerequisites: run the Load chunk.
```{r public_extraction}
public_build_dataset <- "HIVseq"

public_dataset_libraries <- sub("_bamsort_alignment_LTR_D1.csv$", "", basename(
  Sys.glob(file.path(public_paths[[public_build_dataset]]$bamsort,
                     "*_bamsort_alignment_LTR_D1.csv"))))
public_build_list <- union(
  public_maps[[public_build_dataset]] %>%
    filter(condition %in% public_pass) %>% pull(sample),
  public_dataset_libraries[grepl("week0", public_dataset_libraries)]) %>%
  sort()

cat("===", public_build_dataset, "-", length(public_build_list),
    "per-sample objects,", paste(public_pass, collapse = "+"), "pass ===\n")
print(public_qc(public_build_dataset))
print(as.data.frame(public_build_rds(public_build_dataset, public_build_list)))
```

### Integrate
This is a compute-heavy step.
Prerequisites: run the Load chunk.

```{r public_integrate}
public_load_all(public_load_datasets, public_pass, loader = public_extract)
```

### Per-participant DEG
Prerequisites: the Load, Per-sample objects, and Integrate chunks above

Both contrasts within each participant: HIV+ vs HIV- and splice+ vs splice-
among the HIV+ cells. A contrast with fewer than `public_min_cells` cells on
either side is skipped.

```{r public_deg}
for (dataset in public_loaded()) {
  output.dir <- public_datasets[[dataset]]$deg.dir
  dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  public_walk_groups(dataset, function(obj, group) {
    DefaultAssay(obj) <- "RNA"
    obj <- JoinLayers(obj, assay = "RNA")
    tested_genes <- setdiff(rownames(obj[["RNA"]]), public_exclude_genes)

    for (contrast_name in names(public_contrasts)) {
      contrast <- public_contrasts[[contrast_name]]
      obj$deg_group <- contrast$groups(obj)
      n1 <- sum(obj$deg_group == contrast$ident.1, na.rm = TRUE)
      n2 <- sum(obj$deg_group == contrast$ident.2, na.rm = TRUE)
      if (n1 < public_min_cells || n2 < public_min_cells) {
        cat("Skipping", dataset, group, contrast_name,
            "- insufficient cells (", n1, "vs", n2, ")\n")
        next
      }

      Idents(obj) <- "deg_group"
      deg <- FindMarkers(obj,
                         ident.1 = contrast$ident.1, ident.2 = contrast$ident.2,
                         features = tested_genes,
                         assay = "RNA", test.use = "wilcox",
                         logfc.threshold = 0, min.pct = 0.1, verbose = FALSE)
      deg$gene <- rownames(deg)
      write.csv(deg, paste0(output.dir, group, contrast$suffix),
                row.names = FALSE)
      cat("Processed", dataset, group, contrast_name,
          "-", contrast$ident.1, ":", n1, contrast$ident.2, ":", n2, "\n")
    }
  })
}
```

## Plotting

### Print: SIV pathway classes and the public HIV+ signature
In-text numbers for the SIV tier analysis against the public PWH signature.

Prerequisites: the #All SIV `tier_tables`, `tier_deg` and `pathway_scores`,
and #Public Data `public_deg`.
```{r tier_pathways, warning=FALSE}
tier_public_files <- c(
  Sys.glob(paste0(data.root, "Collora/DEG/Viremic_*_DEG_infected.csv")),
  Sys.glob(paste0(data.root, "HIVseq/DEG/Viremic_*_DEG_infected.csv")))
tier_public_min_tables <- 2
tier_pathway_contrasts <- c("GEX_vs_neg", "Both_vs_neg", "CaReOnly_vs_neg",
                            "CaReOnly_vs_GEX", "Union_vs_neg", "GEX_naive")

tier_public_sets <- public_hiv_signature(tier_public_files, tier_fc, tier_pval,
                                         tier_public_min_tables)
cat("=== Public signature from", length(tier_public_files), "tables ===\n")
print(lengths(tier_public_sets))
print(tier_public_sets)

# Reuses the Hallmark list the pathway_scores chunk built
tier_hallmark_sets <- setNames(pathway_hallmark, paste0("HALLMARK_", names(pathway_hallmark)))

tier_rank <- function(deg) {
  stat <- sign(deg$avg_log2FC) * -log10(pmax(deg$p_val, .Machine$double.xmin))
  setNames(stat, deg$gene)
}

tier_pathways <- purrr::map_dfr(names(tier_tables), function(sample_name) {
  purrr::map_dfr(tier_pathway_contrasts, function(contrast_name) {
    deg <- tier_read_deg(tier_deg.dir, sample_name, "all", contrast_name)
    if (is.null(deg)) return(NULL)
    ranks <- tier_rank(deg)
    public_in_universe <- lapply(tier_public_sets, intersect, names(ranks))
    bind_rows(
      fgsea::fgsea(public_in_universe, ranks, minSize = 5, maxSize = 500,
                   nPermSimple = 10000) %>%
        as_tibble() %>% mutate(collection = "Public TenX"),
      fgsea::fgsea(tier_hallmark_sets, ranks, minSize = 10, maxSize = 500,
                   nPermSimple = 10000) %>%
        as_tibble() %>% mutate(collection = "Hallmark",
                               pathway = sub("^HALLMARK_", "", pathway))) %>%
      transmute(sample = sample_name, contrast = contrast_name, collection,
                pathway, NES, padj, size)
  })
})
write.csv(tier_pathways, paste0(tier_deg.dir, "pathways_fgsea.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n=== Public TenX signature in each contrast ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(tier_pathways %>% filter(collection == "Public TenX") %>%
                      arrange(pathway, sample, contrast)))

tier_hallmark <- tier_pathways %>% filter(collection == "Hallmark")
tier_pathway_classes <- purrr::map_dfr(names(tier_reference_contrasts), function(reference_contrast) {
  inner_join(
    tier_hallmark %>% filter(contrast == reference_contrast) %>%
      select(sample, pathway, NES_TenX = NES, padj_TenX = padj),
    tier_hallmark %>% filter(contrast == "CaReOnly_vs_neg") %>%
      select(sample, pathway, NES_CaRe = NES, padj_CaRe = padj),
    by = c("sample", "pathway")) %>%
    mutate(reference = reference_contrast,
           gex_sig  = padj_TenX  < tier_gsea_padj,
           care_sig = padj_CaRe < tier_gsea_padj,
           class = case_when(
             gex_sig & care_sig & sign(NES_TenX) == sign(NES_CaRe) ~ "shared",
             gex_sig & care_sig ~ "discordant",
             gex_sig            ~ "GEX only",
             care_sig           ~ "Ca*Re-added only",
             TRUE               ~ "ns"))
})
cat("\n=== Hallmark pathway classes per sample and TenX reference ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(tier_pathway_classes %>% count(reference, sample, class)))
print(as.data.frame(tier_pathway_classes %>% filter(class != "ns") %>%
                      arrange(reference, sample, class, pathway)))

```

# Giron et al
## Extraction
Downloaded  Giron et al. 2024 (GSE254483) ADT + HTO with our resequenced TenX.

GSE254483 is four hashed pools, HIV-A to HIV-D, each carrying two PWH and two
HIV-uninfected donors. This section analyses the HIV-D pool: it is the only one
that yields HIV RNA+ cells in either arm. Over the whole bamsort window set the
Ca*Re libraries of HIV-D carry 1,457 of the 1,459 HXB2 reads recovered from any
pool, and in the TenX arm HIV-A and HIV-C give 0 HIV RNA+ CD4 T cells against
HIV-D's 2, so the other pools contribute nothing to the Ca*Re-vs-TenX
comparison or to Panel K. HIV-B was not resequenced.

Prerequisites: under `extractionScripts/submissionScripts/Figure3`,
`stepOne_cellranger.sh` (TenX + ADT + hashtags), `stepTwo_bamsort.sh` (HXB2
alignment + splice tables) and `stepThree_process.sh` (per-UMI categories) have
been run, writing to `extractedData/Figure3/singleCell`; and the Public data
`public_load` chunk above has been run, which sets `min_hiv_reads` and
`hiv_tcell_gate` for the `hxb2_per_cell` / `attach_hxb2` helpers this section
reuses.

### Helpers

```{r giron_helpers}
# Donor hashtag -> Scode for the HIV-D pool, resolved against the deposited
# GSE254483 matrix. Its PWH donors are S19/S20 and its HIV-uninfected donors,
# the internal negative control for both arms, are S17/S18.
giron_donors <- tibble::tribble(
  ~pool,   ~hashtag,   ~donor,
  "HIV-D", "Hashtag4", "S19", "HIV-D", "HTO_BD1", "S18",
  "HIV-D", "HTO_BD2",  "S17", "HIV-D", "HTO_BD3", "S20"
) %>%
  mutate(donor_status = ifelse(donor %in% c("S19", "S20"),
                               "PWH", "uninfected"))

# Resolved members of the 12-antibody CITE-seq panel (remaining ADT ids keep
# their cellranger feature names).
giron_adt_map <- c(ADT05 = "CD3", ADT11 = "CD4", ADT08 = "CD8")

# Transcriptome QC for this pool, applied twice: once to choose the barcodes
# the demultiplexers see, and again inside SeuratPipeline. Defined once here so
# the two cannot drift apart.
#   min_features = 500 matches the only filter the authors applied (GSE254483
#     data processing: "filtered cells expressing fewer than 500 genes").
#   max_mito = 5 is the SeuratPipeline default, kept so this pool is cut
#     the same way as every other sample in the paper.
#   max_counts = 10000 tightens the SeuratPipeline default of 20000.
giron_qc <- list(min_features = 500, max_features = 3500,
                 max_counts = 10000, max_mito = 5)

# Barcodes passing that QC, built the way SeuratPipeline builds it so the two
# agree cell for cell.
giron_qc_pass <- function(tenx, pool) {
  q <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = tenx, project = pool, min.cells = 3,
                          min.features = giron_qc$min_features)
  q <- scCustomize::Add_Mito_Ribo(q, species = "Human")
  keep <- q$nFeature_RNA > giron_qc$min_features &
          q$nFeature_RNA < giron_qc$max_features &
          q$nCount_RNA   < giron_qc$max_counts &
          q$percent_mito < giron_qc$max_mito
  colnames(q)[keep]
}

# Seurat replaces underscores in feature names with dashes, so match either form.
giron_features <- function(mat, ids) {
  idx <- match(gsub("_", "-", ids), gsub("_", "-", rownames(mat)))
  stopifnot(!any(is.na(idx)))
  out <- mat[idx, , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(out) <- gsub("_", "-", ids)
  out
}

# One hashed pool -> processed Seurat object of demultiplexed singlets, with
# RNA (human genes), ADT and HTO assays and per-cell donor metadata.
load_giron_pool <- function(pool, counts_root, rds_dir) {
  rds <- file.path(rds_dir, paste0(pool, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(rds)) return(readRDS(rds))

  mtx <- file.path(counts_root, paste0("GRCh38_HXB2_", pool),
                   "outs", "filtered_feature_bc_matrix")
  data <- Read10X(data.dir = mtx)
  tenx <- data[["Gene Expression"]]
  ab  <- data[["Antibody Capture"]]

  donors <- giron_donors[giron_donors$pool == pool, ]
  hto_counts <- giron_features(ab, donors$hashtag)
  # The feature reference carries all 8 hashtags (of all four pools); only the
  # ADT panel belongs in the surface-protein assay.
  adt_counts <- ab[grepl("^ADT", rownames(ab)), , drop = FALSE]
  known <- intersect(names(giron_adt_map), rownames(adt_counts))
  rownames(adt_counts)[match(known, rownames(adt_counts))] <- unname(giron_adt_map[known])

  # demuxmix requires that empty droplets and low-quality cells be removed on
  # their transcriptomic profile before the mixture models are fitted (Klein
  # 2023, Bioinformatics 39:btad481), so the QC cuts come first and both
  # demultiplexers see only the barcodes that survive them.
  qc_pass <- giron_qc_pass(tenx, pool)
  tenx <- tenx[, qc_pass, drop = FALSE]
  hto_counts <- hto_counts[, qc_pass, drop = FALSE]
  adt_counts <- adt_counts[, qc_pass, drop = FALSE]

  demux <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = tenx, project = pool)
  demux[["HTO"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = hto_counts)
  demux[["ADT"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = adt_counts)
  demux <- NormalizeData(demux, assay = "HTO", normalization.method = "CLR",
                         verbose = FALSE)
  demux <- HTODemux(demux, assay = "HTO", positive.quantile = 0.99, verbose = FALSE)
  demux <- NormalizeData(demux, assay = "ADT", normalization.method = "CLR",
                         margin = 2, verbose = FALSE)

  # HTODemux calls each hashtag against its own background, so a droplet can
  # carry a clean top hashtag and still be loaded with ambient antibody from the
  # other donors -- the same ambient that puts Ca*Re molecules on uninfected
  # donors' cells. demuxmix models each hashtag's counts as a negative binomial
  # mixture regressed on the number of detected genes per cell, which separates
  # multiplets and ambiguous droplets from true singlets, so a barcode is kept
  # only if both call it a singlet. The two agree on donor identity for every
  # cell they both keep, so the donor call itself still comes from `hash.ID`.
  # pAcpt is the posterior probability demuxmix requires to accept a call. Its
  # default, 0.9^n_hashtags, relaxes as pools get larger (0.66 for four
  # hashtags); a flat 0.9 applies the same per-hashtag confidence whatever the
  # pool size. It moves the least confident singlets to "uncertain" -- 252 of the
  # 18,010 QC-passing barcodes in HIV-D -- and those are the droplets carrying the most
  # ambient hashtag from the other donors. 0.9, 0.95 and 0.99 all give the same
  # Ca*Re calls, so the result does not hinge on the exact value.
  set.seed(1)
  dmm <- demuxmix::demuxmix(
    as.matrix(GetAssayData(demux, assay = "HTO", layer = "counts")),
    rna = Matrix::colSums(tenx > 0), pAcpt = 0.9)
  dmm_class <- demuxmix::dmmClassify(dmm)[colnames(demux), ]
  clean <- dmm_class$Type == "singlet"

  hash_id <- as.character(demux$hash.ID)
  singlet <- as.character(demux$HTO_classification.global) == "Singlet" & clean
  message(pool, ": ", sum(singlet), " singlets / ", ncol(demux), " QC-passing barcodes (",
          sum(demux$HTO_classification.global == "Doublet"), " HTODemux doublets, ",
          sum(demux$HTO_classification.global == "Negative"), " negative; demuxmix ",
          sum(dmm_class$Type == "multiplet"), " multiplet, ",
          sum(dmm_class$Type == "uncertain"), " uncertain, ",
          sum(dmm_class$Type == "negative"), " negative)")

  # Surface-protein T cell gate: CD3+ by 2-means on the CLR values, CD4 vs CD8.
  # This is the call `adt_cd4t_pass` reads for this pool, so it is the gate
  # behind HIV_status and the Ca*Re call, not just a cell-type label.
  adt_clr <- GetAssayData(demux, assay = "ADT", layer = "data")
  cd3 <- as.numeric(adt_clr["CD3", ]); cd4 <- as.numeric(adt_clr["CD4", ])
  cd8 <- as.numeric(adt_clr["CD8", ])
  set.seed(1)
  km <- kmeans(cd3, centers = 2, nstart = 10)
  cd3_pos <- km$cluster == which.max(km$centers[, 1])
  cell_type_adt <- ifelse(cd3_pos & cd4 > cd8 & cd4 > 0, "CD4_T",
                   ifelse(cd3_pos & cd8 > cd4 & cd8 > 0, "CD8_T",
                   ifelse(cd3_pos, "other_T", "non_T")))
  names(cell_type_adt) <- colnames(demux)
  names(hash_id) <- colnames(demux)

  # Standard human pipeline on the transcriptome of the singlets only. The QC
  # arguments repeat `giron_qc`, which these barcodes already passed, so the cuts
  # are a no-op re-check here and the CD4/CD8 transcript-doublet removal and the
  # normalization/PCA/UMAP steps are what this call contributes.
  #
  # plots = TRUE writes SeuratPipeline's own QC figures (pre/post-QC violins of
  # nFeature_RNA, nCount_RNA and percent_mito, the elbow plot and the UMAP) under
  # <output_dir>/plots/, so a rebuild leaves a record of what the cuts did.
  obj <- SeuratPipeline(tenx[, singlet, drop = FALSE], sample_name = pool,
                        output_dir = dirname(rds_dir), plots = TRUE,
                        rds = FALSE, species = "Human", remove_mac = TRUE,
                        min_features = giron_qc$min_features,
                        max_features = giron_qc$max_features,
                        max_counts   = giron_qc$max_counts,
                        max_mito     = giron_qc$max_mito)

  cells <- colnames(obj)
  obj$pool          <- pool
  hashtag_of_cell   <- unname(hash_id[cells])
  donor_of_hashtag  <- setNames(donors$donor, gsub("_", "-", donors$hashtag))
  status_of_hashtag <- setNames(donors$donor_status, gsub("_", "-", donors$hashtag))
  obj$hashtag       <- hashtag_of_cell
  obj$donor         <- unname(donor_of_hashtag[hashtag_of_cell])
  obj$donor_status  <- unname(status_of_hashtag[hashtag_of_cell])
  obj$cell_type_adt <- unname(cell_type_adt[cells])
  obj$demuxmix_type <- dmm_class$Type[match(cells, colnames(demux))]
  obj$demuxmix_prob <- dmm_class$Prob[match(cells, colnames(demux))]
  obj[["HTO"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = hto_counts[, cells, drop = FALSE])
  obj[["ADT"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = adt_counts[, cells, drop = FALSE])
  obj <- NormalizeData(obj, assay = "HTO", normalization.method = "CLR", verbose = FALSE)
  obj <- NormalizeData(obj, assay = "ADT", normalization.method = "CLR",
                       margin = 2, verbose = FALSE)
  DefaultAssay(obj) <- "RNA"

  dir.create(rds_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(obj, rds)
  obj
}
```

### Per-pool objects
Prerequisite: the Public data `public_load` chunk has been run, for
`min_hiv_reads` and `hiv_tcell_gate`. First run is compute-heavy; reruns read the
cached per-pool RDS.
```{r giron_extraction}
giron_root    <- paste0(data.root, "Figure3/singleCell")
giron_counts  <- file.path(giron_root, "counts")
giron_bamsort <- file.path(giron_root, "bamsort")
giron_rds     <- file.path(giron_root, "Seurat", "RDS")
dir.create(giron_rds, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

giron_pools <- "HIV-D"

giron_objs <- lapply(giron_pools, function(pool) {
  obj <- load_giron_pool(pool, giron_counts, giron_rds)
  obj$orig.ident <- pool
  obj <- RenameCells(obj, add.cell.id = pool)
  attach_hxb2(obj, pool, giron_bamsort)
})
names(giron_objs) <- giron_pools

# One row per donor.
giron_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(giron_objs, function(obj) {
  tibble(pool         = obj$pool,
         donor        = obj$donor,
         donor_status = obj$donor_status,
         cd4_T        = obj$CD4_Tcell,
         hiv          = obj$HIV_status == "HIV+")
}) %>%
  group_by(pool, donor, donor_status) %>%
  summarize(n_cells = n(), cd4_T = sum(cd4_T), HIV_RNA_pos_cells = sum(hiv),
            .groups = "drop") %>%

    "HXB2 reads/cell (by donor) ===\n")
```

### Ca*Re
`D__UMI_read_counts_full.csv` from `Figure3/CaRe/bamsort/reads/`. The pool was
probed with five Ca*Re libraries (`D_D1`, `_D4`, `_env`, `_nef`, `_pol`);
stepThree gathers all five into one per-UMI table, resolves multi-mapped UMIs
and filters to the pool's raw cellIDs, so no per-library summing is needed here. This chunk
applies the detection thresholds and the CD4 T gate, and attaches the result to
each pool's object as metadata.
Prerequisite: `stepTwo_bamsort_CaRe.sh` + `stepThree_process_CaRe.sh` under
`extractionScripts/submissionScripts/Figure3` have been run, plus
the `giron_extraction` chunk above.
```{r giron_care}
giron_care_dir <- paste0(data.root,
                          "Figure3/CaRe/bamsort/reads/")
giron_care_pool <- c(D_ = "HIV-D")
giron_care_cols <- c("US", "US.SS", "SS.MS", "SS", "MS", "any", "total")

# Detection thresholds. Set here rather than in the pipeline so they can be
# varied without re-running stepThree.
#
# Read counts are distinct reads: stepTwo charges a read spanning two adjacent
# junction windows to one of them (`primary_count`), so min_reads means what it
# says. Under the old summed counts every D1-probe molecule was doubled and
# min_reads = 5 was really 2.5.
#
# The two HIV-uninfected donors multiplexed into the pool are the internal
# negative control, and the threshold is set to the point where they are empty.
# At min_umi = 1 that point is min_reads = 4; 4, 5 and 6 all return the same
# four PWH cells, so 5 is used to keep a step of margin rather than sitting on
# the boundary of the control. Requiring a second UMI instead would leave one
# PWH cell of the four, so the read threshold is the cheaper way to the same
# specificity now that ambient droplets are removed upstream by demuxmix and
# the CD4 T gate is applied to this arm as well as the TenX arm.
giron_care_min_reads <- 5   # min reads to keep a UMI
giron_care_min_umi   <- 1   # min UMIs to call a cell Ca*Re+

read_giron_care <- function(pool) {
  empty <- setNames(rep(list(numeric()), length(giron_care_cols)), giron_care_cols)
  empty <- tibble::as_tibble(c(list(cellID = character()), empty))

  token <- names(giron_care_pool)[match(pool, giron_care_pool)]
  f <- file.path(giron_care_dir, paste0(token, "_UMI_read_counts_full.csv"))
  # stepThree writes no file for a pool with no HXB2 reads in any region.
  if (!file.exists(f)) {
    message("CaRe: no stepThree table for ", pool, " (", basename(f), ")")
    return(empty)
  }

  d <- set_minimums("CaRe", f,
                      min_reads = giron_care_min_reads,
                      min_umi   = giron_care_min_umi,
                      save_valid_umi = FALSE)
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty)

  # set_minimums names categories "US-SS"/"SS-MS"; read.csv would have made
  # those "US.SS"/"SS.MS", which is what the rest of this section expects.
  names(d) <- gsub("-", ".", names(d), fixed = TRUE)
  for (cc in giron_care_cols) if (!cc %in% names(d)) d[[cc]] <- 0
  d %>%
    mutate(cellID = paste0(pool, "_", as.character(cellID))) %>%
    select(cellID, dplyr::all_of(giron_care_cols))
}

# Attach the pooled CaRe counts to each per-pool object. Ca*Re is called on the
# same population as the TenX arm: `attach_hxb2` zeroes the HXB2 columns outside
# the CD4 T gate before calling HIV_status, so the CaRe columns are zeroed
# there too and the two arms are counted over the same cells.
giron_objs <- lapply(giron_pools, function(pool) {
  obj <- giron_objs[[pool]]
  care <- read_giron_care(pool)
  m <- match(colnames(obj), care$cellID)
  pick <- function(col) ifelse(is.na(m) | !obj$CD4_Tcell, 0, care[[col]][m])
  obj$CaRe       <- pick("total")
  obj$CaRe_US    <- pick("US")
  obj$CaRe_US.SS <- pick("US.SS")
  obj$CaRe_SS.MS <- pick("SS.MS")
  obj$CaRe_SS    <- pick("SS")
  obj$CaRe_MS    <- pick("MS")
  obj$CaRe_any   <- pick("any")
  obj$CaRe_status <- ifelse(obj$CaRe > 0, "CaRe+", "CaRe-")
  obj
})
names(giron_objs) <- giron_pools

giron_care_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(giron_objs, function(obj) {
  tibble(pool  = obj$pool,
         donor = obj$donor,
         care = obj$CaRe_status == "CaRe+",
         hiv   = obj$HIV_status == "HIV+")
}) %>%
  group_by(pool, donor) %>%
  summarize(n_cells = n(), CaRe_pos_cells = sum(care),
            TenX_HIV_pos_cells = sum(hiv), both = sum(care & hiv),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(pool, donor)

cat("=== Giron et al. CaRe (EGS026, 5 probes pooled;",
    ">=", giron_care_min_reads, "reads/UMI, >=", giron_care_min_umi,
    "UMIs/cell) ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(giron_care_summary))
```

### Print: detection against the pool's HIV-uninfected donors
In-text sentence for the specificity of the viral-RNA call. The HIV-D pool
multiplexes two PWH with two HIV-uninfected donors, so the uninfected pair is an
internal negative control that went through the same droplets, the same library
and the same bamsort window set as the PWH pair: a false positive from ambient
virion RNA or from index hopping would have to land on them too. Both arms are
counted over the gated CD4 T cells, which is the population `attach_hxb2` and
the Ca*Re attachment both zero outside.
Prerequisites: the `giron_extraction` and `giron_care` chunks above.
```{r giron_negative_control}
giron_control <- purrr::map_dfr(giron_objs, function(obj)
  tibble(donor_status = obj$donor_status, donor = obj$donor,
         cd4_T = obj$CD4_Tcell,
         GEX  = obj$HIV_status  == "HIV+",
         CaRe = obj$CaRe_status == "CaRe+")) %>%
  filter(cd4_T) %>%
  group_by(donor_status) %>%
  summarize(donors = n_distinct(donor), cd4_T = n(),
            GEX_pos = sum(GEX), CaRe_pos = sum(CaRe), .groups = "drop")

cat("=== Giron HIV-D, gated CD4 T cells by donor status ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(giron_control), row.names = FALSE)

# The sentence is emitted per arm rather than once, because the positive call is
# the TenX one in one arm and the Ca*Re one in the other, and the two differ on
# the PWH donors even though both are empty on the controls.
giron_control_arms <- c(GEX = "TenX|HIV RNA+", CaRe = "Ca*Re|Ca*Re+")
giron_control_sentence <- function(arm) {
  label <- strsplit(giron_control_arms[[arm]], "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  neg <- giron_control[giron_control$donor_status == "uninfected", ]
  pwh <- giron_control[giron_control$donor_status == "PWH", ]
  cat(sprintf(
    "%s: %d %s / %s CD4+ T cells from %d HIV-negative individuals, versus %d / %s from %d PWH\n",
    label[1], neg[[paste0(arm, "_pos")]], label[2],
    format(neg$cd4_T, big.mark = ","), neg$donors,
    pwh[[paste0(arm, "_pos")]], format(pwh$cd4_T, big.mark = ","), pwh$donors))
}
cat("\n")
invisible(lapply(names(giron_control_arms), giron_control_sentence))
```



# ART comparison

## Extraction
### Per-cell table

Prerequisites: `public_load` (for `public_paths`, `public_maps`), the ART
per-sample objects from `public_extraction`, the `public_deg` Viremic tables,
`giron_extraction` and `giron_care`, and the `tier_tables` chunk for
`D195_tiers.csv`. Loads every per-sample object in turn, so run on a compute
node.
```{r art_cells}
art.dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure3/ARTcompare/")
dir.create(art.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
art_cells_file <- paste0(art.dir, "art_cd4t_cells.rds")

art_hallmark_sets <- c("OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION", "GLYCOLYSIS", "MTORC1_SIGNALING",
                       "INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE", "INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE",
                       "TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB", "INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE")
art_public_files <- c(
  Sys.glob(paste0(data.root, "Collora/DEG/Viremic_*_DEG_infected.csv")),
  Sys.glob(paste0(data.root, "HIVseq/DEG/Viremic_*_DEG_infected.csv")))
art_gene_sets <- c(cd4t_subset_markers,
                   hallmark_gene_sets()[art_hallmark_sets],
                   public_hiv_signature(art_public_files, fc = 0.5, pval = 0.01,
                                        min_tables = 2)["PUBLIC_HIV_UP"])

# Viral features are left out of host library size and gene sets
art_viral_feature <- function(genes) genes == "HXB2" | grepl("mac239", genes, ignore.case = TRUE)

# Host library size and module scores over one object's CD4 T cells
art_score_cd4 <- function(obj, cells) {
  DefaultAssay(obj) <- "RNA"
  obj <- subset(obj, cells = cells)
  if (inherits(obj[["RNA"]], "Assay5")) obj <- JoinLayers(obj, assay = "RNA")
  counts <- GetAssayData(obj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  host <- !art_viral_feature(rownames(counts))
  obj <- NormalizeData(obj, assay = "RNA", verbose = FALSE)
  present <- lapply(art_gene_sets, intersect, rownames(counts)[host])
  usable <- names(present)[lengths(present) >= 3]
  obj <- AddModuleScore(obj, features = present[usable], assay = "RNA",
                        name = "art_score", seed = 1, search = FALSE)
  scores <- obj@meta.data[, paste0("art_score", seq_along(usable)), drop = FALSE]
  colnames(scores) <- usable
  bind_cols(tibble(cellID   = colnames(obj),
                   nCount   = Matrix::colSums(counts[host, ]),
                   nFeature = Matrix::colSums(counts[host, ] > 0)),
            as_tibble(scores))
}

# HXB2 UMIs of a human object, and whether any is spliced
art_hxb2_umis <- function(md) {
  md$HXB2_US + md$HXB2_US.SS + md$HXB2_SS.MS + md$HXB2_SS + md$HXB2_MS + md$HXB2_any
}

if (file.exists(art_cells_file)) {
  art_cells <- readRDS(art_cells_file)
} else {
  art_giron <- purrr::map_dfr(giron_pools, function(pool) {
    obj <- giron_objs[[pool]]
    cd4 <- colnames(obj)[obj$CD4_Tcell]
    md <- obj@meta.data[cd4, ]
    art_score_cd4(obj, cd4) %>%
      mutate(dataset = "Giron", reference_group = md$donor,
             donor_status = md$donor_status,
             GEX_called  = md$HIV_status == "HIV+", CaRe_called = md$CaRe_status == "CaRe+",
             GEX_UMIs    = art_hxb2_umis(md),       CaRe_UMIs   = md$CaRe,
             GEX_spliced = md$HXB2_SS.MS + md$HXB2_SS + md$HXB2_MS > 0,
             CaRe_spliced = md$CaRe_SS.MS + md$CaRe_SS + md$CaRe_MS > 0)
  })

  art_public <- purrr::map_dfr(c("Collora", "HIVseq"), function(dataset) {
    paths <- public_paths[[dataset]]
    libraries <- public_maps[[dataset]] %>% filter(condition == "ART")
    purrr::map_dfr(libraries$sample, function(sample) {
      obj <- load_human_sample(sample, paths$counts, paths$rds, qc = public_qc(dataset))
      obj$orig.ident <- sample
      obj <- attach_hxb2(RenameCells(obj, add.cell.id = sample), sample,
                         paths$bamsort, rule = public_hiv_rule(dataset))
      cd4 <- colnames(obj)[obj$CD4_Tcell]
      md <- obj@meta.data[cd4, ]
      out <- art_score_cd4(obj, cd4) %>%
        mutate(dataset = dataset, reference_group = sample, donor_status = "PWH",
               GEX_called  = md$HIV_status == "HIV+", CaRe_called = FALSE,
               GEX_UMIs    = art_hxb2_umis(md),       CaRe_UMIs   = 0,
               GEX_spliced = md$HXB2_SS.MS + md$HXB2_SS + md$HXB2_MS > 0,
               CaRe_spliced = FALSE)
      rm(obj); gc()
      out
    })
  })

  art_d195_tiers <- read.csv(paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                                    "combined/tiers/D195_tiers.csv")) %>%
    mutate(cellID = as.character(cellID))
  art_d195_obj <- readRDS(paste0(data.root, "Figure1/",
                                 "singleCell/Seurat/RDS/D195.rds"))
  art_d195 <- art_score_cd4(art_d195_obj, intersect(art_d195_tiers$cellID, colnames(art_d195_obj)))
  rm(art_d195_obj); gc()
  tiers_m <- art_d195_tiers[match(art_d195$cellID, art_d195_tiers$cellID), ]
  art_d195 <- art_d195 %>%
    mutate(dataset = "SIV D195", reference_group = "D195", donor_status = "SIV+ ART",
           GEX_called  = tiers_m$tier %in% c("both", "GEX_only"),
           CaRe_called = tiers_m$tier %in% c("both", "CaRe_only"),
           GEX_UMIs    = tiers_m$GEX_UMIs, CaRe_UMIs = tiers_m$care_UMIs,
           GEX_spliced = tiers_m$GEX_spliced, CaRe_spliced = tiers_m$care_spliced)

  art_cells <- bind_rows(art_giron, art_public, art_d195) %>%
    mutate(positive = GEX_called | CaRe_called)
  saveRDS(art_cells, art_cells_file)
}

cat("=== CD4 T cells and positives per dataset ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(art_cells %>% group_by(dataset) %>%
  summarize(CD4_T = n(), reference_groups = n_distinct(reference_group),
            GEX = sum(GEX_called), CaRe = sum(CaRe_called), positives = sum(positive))),
  row.names = FALSE)
```

## Plotting
### Panel K: host state of the HIV RNA+ cells on ART

Prerequisites: the `art_cells` chunk.
```{r art_set_level}
art_panel.dir  <- paste0(plot.root, "Figure3/")
dir.create(art_panel.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
art_nperm <- 10000
set.seed(1)

art_features <- c("nCount", "nFeature", names(cd4t_subset_markers), art_hallmark_sets,
                  "PUBLIC_HIV_UP")
art_feature_labels <- c(nCount = "host UMIs", nFeature = "host genes",
                        naive_Tcm = "naive/Tcm", Tem = "Tem", cytotoxic = "cytotoxic",
                        Treg = "Treg", cycling = "cycling",
                        OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION = "OxPhos", GLYCOLYSIS = "Glycolysis",
                        MTORC1_SIGNALING = "mTORC1", INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE = "IFN-gamma",
                        INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE = "IFN-alpha",
                        TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB = "TNFA/NFkB",
                        INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE = "Inflammatory",
                        PUBLIC_HIV_UP = "viremic HIV+ signature")
art_human <- c("Giron", "Collora", "HIVseq")
art_levels <- c(art_human, "SIV D195", "Human pooled")
art_dataset_colors <- c(Giron = "#1baf7a", public_dataset_colors, `SIV D195` = "#9B8579")
art_panel_features <- c("naive_Tcm", "Tem", "cytotoxic", "INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE",
                        "TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB", "INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE")

art_pct <- art_cells
for (f in art_features) {
  art_pct[[paste0("pct_", f)]] <- within_group_percentile(art_pct[[f]], art_pct$reference_group)
}
art_level_cells <- function(level) {
  if (level == "Human pooled") filter(art_pct, dataset %in% art_human)
  else filter(art_pct, dataset == level)
}

art_set_tests <- purrr::map_dfr(art_levels, function(level) {
  df <- art_level_cells(level)
  purrr::map_dfr(art_features, function(f) {
    values <- df[[paste0("pct_", f)]]
    observed <- mean(values[df$positive])
    null <- matched_mean_null(values, df$reference_group, df$positive, art_nperm)
    tibble(level = level, feature = f, n_pos = sum(df$positive), mean_pct = observed,
           null_mean = mean(null), null_sd = stats::sd(null),
           null_lo = quantile(null, 0.025), null_hi = quantile(null, 0.975),
           p = min(1, 2 * min(mean(null >= observed), mean(null <= observed))))
  }) %>% mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, "BH"))
}) %>%
  # The positives' mean in SD of its own null. The null's width is set by the
  # number of positives, so this is what makes a value comparable between a
  # level with 5 positives and one with 42; the panel fills on it.
  mutate(z = (mean_pct - null_mean) / null_sd)
cat("=== Positives' mean within-group percentile vs group-matched draws ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(art_set_tests %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean_pct, null_mean, null_sd, null_lo, null_hi, z), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         across(c(p, p_adj), ~ signif(.x, 2)))), row.names = FALSE)

# Human positives against SIV positives directly, two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum
# on the within-group percentiles, BH across the same 15 features. Printed and
# written out but NOT drawn: the panel's mark is the per-group matched-draw
# test, so each row is read against its own null and not against the other
# row. Marking this comparison on the plot would invite reading the panel as a
# demonstrated between-group difference, and none of the six plotted
# signatures reaches significance here. It is kept because that is exactly the
# caveat the contrast needs, and because the test treats cells as independent
# while the human side spans donors and libraries and the SIV side is one
# animal.
art_between <- purrr::map_dfr(art_features, function(f) {
  col <- paste0("pct_", f)
  human <- art_level_cells("Human pooled") %>% filter(positive)
  siv   <- art_level_cells("SIV D195")     %>% filter(positive)
  tibble(feature = f, n_human = nrow(human), n_siv = nrow(siv),
         mean_human = mean(human[[col]]), mean_siv = mean(siv[[col]]),
         p = wilcox.test(human[[col]], siv[[col]])$p.value)
}) %>% mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, "BH"))
cat("\n=== human ART positives vs SIV ART positives (Wilcoxon on percentiles) ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(art_between %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean_human, mean_siv), ~ round(.x, 3)),
         across(c(p, p_adj), ~ signif(.x, 2)))), row.names = FALSE)

# Main panel: the six signatures across the x axis, the pooled human positives
# and the SIV ART sample as the two rows. Both are percentiles within the
# cell's own donor or library, which is what puts two species and two
# chemistries on a common scale.
#
# The tile is filled by z, the positives' mean in SD of its own matched-draw
# null, and not by the raw mean. The null's width is set by the number of
# positives, 23 against 42 here, so a raw-percentile fill would give the same
# colour to two cells carrying different evidence. The printed number is the
# raw mean percentile, so both quantities are on the tile.
art_panel_levels <- c("Human pooled", "SIV D195")
art_panel_labels <- c(`Human pooled` = "human pooled", `SIV D195` = "SIV ART (D195)")
art_z_limit <- 3.5

art_row_labels <- setNames(
  sprintf("%s\nn = %d", art_panel_labels[art_panel_levels],
          art_set_tests$n_pos[match(art_panel_levels, art_set_tests$level)]),
  art_panel_levels)

art_panel_tiles <- art_set_tests %>%
  filter(level %in% art_panel_levels, feature %in% art_panel_features) %>%
  mutate(row = factor(art_row_labels[level], levels = rev(art_row_labels)),
         feature_label = factor(art_feature_labels[feature],
                                levels = art_feature_labels[art_panel_features]),
         star = ifelse(p_adj < 0.05, "*", ""))

art_pooled_plot <- ggplot(art_panel_tiles, aes(feature_label, row, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.4) +
  # A BH-significant cell carries a heavy outline as well as the asterisk, so
  # the mark reads in greyscale and at panel size.
  geom_tile(data = filter(art_panel_tiles, p_adj < 0.05), fill = NA,
            color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f%s", mean_pct, star)), size = 2.9) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       limits = c(-art_z_limit, art_z_limit), oob = scales::squish,
                       breaks = c(-art_z_limit, 0, art_z_limit),
                       labels = c(sprintf("%.1f (depleted)", -art_z_limit), "0",
                                  sprintf("+%.1f (enriched)", art_z_limit)),
                       name = "SD from null",
                       guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top",
                                              title.hjust = 0.5)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       subtitle = paste("HIV/SIV RNA+ CD4 T cells on ART; cell = their mean percentile among",
                        "the CD4 T cells of the\nsame donor / library, fill = that mean in SD of",
                        sprintf("%s group-matched draws of the same\nnumber of negatives;",
                                format(art_nperm, big.mark = ",")),
                        "outline and * = BH p < 0.05 across the 15 features of that row")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7.5),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5, lineheight = 0.95, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.height = unit(0.22, "cm"),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 7), legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.margin = margin(t = -2),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6.6, hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.1,
                                     margin = margin(b = 4)),
        plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 2, 4))
ggsave(paste0(art_panel.dir, "PanelK_ART_hostState.pdf"), art_pooled_plot,
       width = 6.6, height = 2.5)
write.csv(art_between, paste0(art_panel.dir, "PanelK_ART_humanVsSIV_tests.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(art_set_tests, paste0(art_panel.dir, "PanelK_ART_hostState_tests.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
print(art_pooled_plot)

# Supp Fig 3 Panel H draws every feature at every level from the tests
# written just above; it is made in SuppFigs.Rmd
# (`suppfig3_panelH_art_features`).
```

### Print: viral load of the ART macaque against the acute samples

Prerequisites: the `tier_tables` chunk has written `<sample>_tiers.csv`, and
stepOne cellranger has written `metrics_summary.csv` for each sample's Ca*Re and
TenX libraries
```{r art_load_depth_normalised}
artload_group <- c(D195 = "ART", Invitro = "invitro", Pacute = "viremia", W2 = "viremia")
artload_reference <- c("Invitro", "Pacute", "W2")
# Viral UMIs per cell per this many reads per cell
artload_per_reads <- 1e4

artload_metric <- function(file, field) {
  metrics <- read.csv(file, check.names = FALSE)
  as.numeric(gsub(",", "", metrics[[field]][1]))
}
artload_care_reads <- function(sample_name) {
  files <- Sys.glob(paste0(data.root, "Figure1/CaRe/", artload_group[[sample_name]],
                           "/counts/Mmul_10_mac239_", sample_name,
                           "_*/outs/metrics_summary.csv"))
  if (length(files) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  sum(vapply(files, artload_metric, numeric(1), "Number of Reads"))
}
artload_tenx_reads <- function(sample_name) {
  file <- paste0(data.root, "Figure1/singleCell/counts/outs_", sample_name,
                 "/metrics_summary.csv")
  if (!file.exists(file)) return(NA_real_)
  artload_metric(file, "Number of Reads")
}

artload_tiers <- read_tier_tables(paste0(data.root, "Figure1/combined/tiers/"),
                                  names(artload_group))
artload_table <- purrr::map_dfr(names(artload_group), function(sample_name) {
  tiers <- artload_tiers[[sample_name]]
  if (is.null(tiers)) { cat("missing tier table:", sample_name, "\n"); return(NULL) }
  umis <- list(`Ca*Re` = tiers$care_UMIs, TenX = tiers$GEX_UMIs)
  reads <- c(`Ca*Re` = artload_care_reads(sample_name),
             TenX    = artload_tenx_reads(sample_name))
  purrr::map_dfr(names(umis), function(arm_name) {
    reads_per_cell <- reads[[arm_name]] / nrow(tiers)
    tibble(sample = sample_name, arm = arm_name, cells = nrow(tiers),
           positive = sum(umis[[arm_name]] > 0), max_umi = max(umis[[arm_name]]),
           reads = reads[[arm_name]], reads_per_cell = reads_per_cell,
           max_per_reads = artload_per_reads * max(umis[[arm_name]]) / reads_per_cell)
  })
})

cat(sprintf(paste0("=== Maximum viral UMIs per CD4 T cell, raw and per %s reads",
                   " per cell ===\n"), format(artload_per_reads, big.mark = ",",
                                              scientific = FALSE)))
print(as.data.frame(artload_table %>%
  transmute(sample, arm, cells, positive, max_umi,
            reads = format(reads, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
            reads_per_cell = round(reads_per_cell),
            max_per_reads = round(max_per_reads, 2))), row.names = FALSE)

for (arm_name in unique(artload_table$arm)) {
  art  <- artload_table %>% filter(arm == arm_name, sample == "D195")
  rest <- artload_table %>% filter(arm == arm_name, sample %in% artload_reference)
  top_raw  <- rest[which.max(rest$max_umi), ]
  top_norm <- rest[which.max(rest$max_per_reads), ]
  cat(sprintf(paste0("\n%s: ART (D195) %d UMIs in its highest cell, %.2f per %s reads",
                     " per cell\n  (%s positive cells of %s gated, %s reads = %s per",
                     " cell).\n  Highest elsewhere: %s %d UMIs (%.1fx ART) raw, %s %.2f",
                     " per %s reads per cell (%.1fx ART).\n"),
              arm_name, art$max_umi, art$max_per_reads,
              format(artload_per_reads, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
              format(art$positive, big.mark = ","), format(art$cells, big.mark = ","),
              format(art$reads, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
              format(round(art$reads_per_cell), big.mark = ","),
              top_raw$sample, top_raw$max_umi, top_raw$max_umi / art$max_umi,
              top_norm$sample, top_norm$max_per_reads,
              format(artload_per_reads, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
              top_norm$max_per_reads / art$max_per_reads))
}
rm(arm_name, art, rest, top_raw, top_norm)
```


# Viral load vs splice status
Per-cell viral load of every HIV/SIV RNA+ CD4 T cell, split by whether any of
its viral molecules is spliced, with the viremic and the ART-suppressed donors
side by side. Built in the style of Supp Fig 2 Panel E (the SIV version of the
same comparison), so the human datasets and D195 are read off one axis.

Viral load is **UMIs**, not reads: `hxb2` is a read count (it is what the
`reads` HIV+ rule tests), while the isoform columns `US / US.SS / SS / MS /
SS.MS / any` written by `hxb2_per_cell` are counts of distinct (cell, UMI)
pairs, so `art_hxb2_umis` sums them to the cell's viral UMI count. splice+ is
`SS + MS + SS.MS > 0`, the same rule as `public_sample_table` and Supp Fig 2
Panel E: SS-MS is the {SS, MS} set, so the molecule is certainly spliced and
only its splice count is unresolved. SS is unreachable in the HXB2 arm (no
region in `hiv_region_category` emits it and the splice override emits only
MS / SS.MS), so for the human 10X data the rule reduces to `MS + SS.MS > 0`;
it is written out in full so the SIV and HIV arms carry one definition.

## Extraction
### Viremic per-cell table
The viremic counterpart of `art_cells`: one row per CD4 T cell of the Collora
and HIV-seq viremic libraries, with its viral UMI count and splice status. No
module scores are computed here -- this panel needs only the viral columns --
so the table is built straight from `load_human_sample` + `attach_hxb2` rather
than through `art_score_cd4`. Cached to
`extractedData/Figure3/loadSplice/viremic_cd4t_cells.rds`; delete it to rebuild.
Prerequisites: `public_load` (for `public_paths`, `public_maps`, `public_qc`,
`min_hiv_reads` and `hiv_tcell_gate`), the per-sample Seurat objects under each
dataset's `rds` directory, and the `art_cells` chunk for `art_hxb2_umis`.
Loads 18 per-sample objects in turn, so run on a compute node.
```{r viremic_cells}
loadsplice.dir <- paste0(data.root, "Figure3/loadSplice/")
dir.create(loadsplice.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
viremic_cells_file <- paste0(loadsplice.dir, "viremic_cd4t_cells.rds")

if (file.exists(viremic_cells_file)) {
  viremic_cells <- readRDS(viremic_cells_file)
} else {
  viremic_cells <- purrr::map_dfr(c("Collora", "HIVseq"), function(dataset) {
    libraries <- public_maps[[dataset]] %>% filter(condition == "Viremic")
    paths <- public_paths[[dataset]]
    purrr::map_dfr(libraries$sample, function(sample) {
      obj <- load_human_sample(sample, paths$counts, paths$rds, qc = public_qc(dataset))
      obj$orig.ident <- sample
      obj <- attach_hxb2(RenameCells(obj, add.cell.id = sample), sample,
                         paths$bamsort, rule = public_hiv_rule(dataset))
      md <- obj@meta.data[obj$CD4_Tcell, , drop = FALSE]
      out <- tibble(
        cellID = rownames(md), dataset = dataset, reference_group = sample,
        participant  = libraries$participant[match(sample, libraries$sample)],
        donor_status = "PWH",
        GEX_called   = md$HIV_status == "HIV+", CaRe_called = FALSE,
        GEX_UMIs     = art_hxb2_umis(md),       CaRe_UMIs   = 0,
        GEX_spliced  = md$HXB2_SS.MS + md$HXB2_SS + md$HXB2_MS > 0,
        CaRe_spliced = FALSE)
      rm(obj); gc()
      out
    })
  }) %>% mutate(positive = GEX_called | CaRe_called)
  saveRDS(viremic_cells, viremic_cells_file)
}

cat("=== viremic CD4 T cells and HIV RNA+ calls per dataset ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(viremic_cells %>% group_by(dataset) %>%
  summarize(libraries = n_distinct(reference_group), participants = n_distinct(participant),
            CD4_T = n(), HIV_pos = sum(GEX_called),
            splice_pos = sum(GEX_called & GEX_spliced))), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Plotting
### Panel J: viral load of splice+ and splice- cells, viremic vs ART
One point per HIV/SIV RNA+ CD4 T cell, x = dataset and detection arm, y = that
cell's viral UMIs on a log10 axis, coloured by splice status, faceted into the
viremic and the ART-suppressed donors. A boxplot is drawn only where a splice
group holds at least `loadsplice_min_box` cells, so a group too small for
quartiles to land on real observations shows its cells and nothing else. No
statistic depends on that cut: the tests and summaries below are computed
over every called cell regardless of what is drawn. Where a group has both splice groups the annotation is
the difference in mean viral UMIs and a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of
viral UMIs between them; where it has no splice+ cell the annotation says so,
as in Supp Fig 2 Panel E.

Two summaries are printed alongside the panel, both over the viremic cells.
The first is the splice+ **rate** per viral load bin (`loadsplice_bins`,
doubling in width so the axis is even on a log scale), which measures how
splice detection tracks load across the whole range. The second,
`pct_neg_at_min_pos` in the stats table, is the share of a group's splice-
cells whose load reaches the lowest load any splice+ cell of that same group
carries: the exclusivity check, where 0 means the two splice groups do not
overlap in load at all and 100 means the splice+ range spans the whole
splice- range. The rate is the one to quote, because a single splice+ cell at
the bottom of the axis sets the minimum and with it `pct_neg_at_min_pos`,
while the rate is computed over every cell in every bin.

The dashed horizontal line is the low/high viral load boundary, taken from
Panel C's `tier_binload_cut` rather than fitted again here, so "high load"
means one thing across the figure. It is carried across both facets, so the
ART cells are read against the boundary the viremic cells set.

Panel C fits that cut as the trough of a two-component Gaussian mixture on
log2 load in the SIV Ca*Re samples. The same procedure on these human 10X
cells is what licenses reusing it: log2 load is bimodal pooled (Hartigan dip
D = 0.049, p < 0.001), a two-component mixture beats one (BIC -2460 vs -3282)
with component means at 1.2 and 70.6 UMIs, and the density trough falls at
10.7 UMIs pooled and 8.5 in Collora alone. The shared cut sits inside that
range. The two are not the same measurement -- Panel C's is Ca*Re UMIs in SIV,
this axis is mostly 10X HXB2 UMIs in human -- so the shared number is a
convention supported by the troughs coinciding, not by the scales being equal.

Because it is a convention, the chunk checks it rather than assuming it: viral
UMIs are swept as a `>= cut` rule for calling a viremic cell splice+, scored by
Youden's J (sensitivity + specificity - 1), and the chunk prints J, sensitivity
and specificity at the boundary next to what these cells alone would choose and
the range of cuts within 0.01 J of that. max-F1 is not used: splice+ prevalence
among the viremic HIV+ cells is low enough that F1 optimises precision and
lands far up the load axis rather than where the two splice groups separate.

Prerequisite for the boundary: the `tier_binary_load` chunk, which defines
`tier_binload_cut`. The chunk stops rather than drawing a second, different
boundary if it has not run.

The HIV-seq arm is the Primer libraries only, because `public_maps$HIVseq`
is filtered to `grepl("Primer$", ...)` in `public_load`, as everywhere else
in this figure. The week0 NOTHING libraries are the chemistry control and are
compared against Primer in SuppFigs.Rmd's `public_primer_vs_nothing` chunk,
not here.

Writes `PanelJ_loadVsSplice.pdf` and `PanelJ_loadVsSplice_stats.csv` to the
Figure3 plot directory.
Prerequisites: the `art_cells` and `viremic_cells` chunks.
```{r panelJ_load_splice}
output.dir <- paste0(plot.root, "Figure3/")
dir.create(output.dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Cells in a splice group before a boxplot is drawn. 5 is where ggplot's
# quantile(type = 7) hinges stop being interpolations and land on actual
# observations again (Q1 = x[2], Q3 = x[4]); below it the box collapses
# towards the range and restates the points with extra ink. No statistic
# depends on this -- loadsplice_stats is computed over every cell either way,
# and the jittered points show the whole group whether or not it gets a box.
loadsplice_min_box <- 5

# One arm of a per-cell table, restricted to the cells that arm called.
loadsplice_arm <- function(df, arm, condition) {
  tenx <- arm == "10X"
  tibble(dataset         = df$dataset,
         reference_group = df$reference_group,
         condition       = condition,
         arm             = arm,
         called          = if (tenx) df$GEX_called  else df$CaRe_called,
         viral_UMIs      = if (tenx) df$GEX_UMIs    else df$CaRe_UMIs,
         splice_group    = ifelse(if (tenx) df$GEX_spliced else df$CaRe_spliced,
                                  "splice+", "splice-")) %>%
    filter(called) %>% select(-called)
}

loadsplice_cells <- bind_rows(
  loadsplice_arm(viremic_cells, "10X",   "viremic"),
  loadsplice_arm(art_cells,     "10X",   "ART"),
  loadsplice_arm(art_cells,     "Ca*Re", "ART"))

# Arms a dataset never ran call no cells, so they drop out here rather than
# being listed by hand.
loadsplice_labels <- c(Collora = "Collora", HIVseq = "HIV-seq", Giron = "Giron",
                       `SIV D195` = "SIV D195")
loadsplice_order <- c("Collora", "HIVseq", "Giron", "SIV D195")
loadsplice_cells <- loadsplice_cells %>%
  mutate(group = paste0(loadsplice_labels[dataset], "\n", arm),
         dataset = factor(dataset, levels = loadsplice_order),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = c("viremic", "ART"))) %>%
  arrange(condition, dataset, arm) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = unique(group)),
         splice_group = factor(splice_group, levels = c("splice-", "splice+")))

# A called cell with no viral UMI would be dropped silently by the log axis.
stopifnot(all(loadsplice_cells$viral_UMIs > 0))

# splice+ rate against viral load, over the viremic cells of both datasets.
# The rate is the load-vs-splicing summary to quote rather than the lowest
# load of a splice+ cell: one such cell anywhere low on the axis fixes that
# minimum, while the rate is computed over every cell in every bin. Bins
# double in width so the axis is even on a log scale, as in the burden
# panels above.
loadsplice_bins <- c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, Inf)
loadsplice_bin_labels <- c("1", "2", "3-4", "5-8", "9-16", "17-32", "33-64",
                           "65-128", ">128")
loadsplice_rate <- loadsplice_cells %>%
  filter(condition == "viremic") %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(viral_UMIs, loadsplice_bins, labels = loadsplice_bin_labels)) %>%
  group_by(group, bin) %>%
  summarize(cells = n(), splice_pos = sum(splice_group == "splice+"),
            rate = 100 * mean(splice_group == "splice+"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(cells > 0)
cat("=== viremic splice+ rate by viral load bin ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(loadsplice_rate %>% mutate(rate = round(rate, 1),
        group = gsub("\n", " ", group))), row.names = FALSE)

# Low/high viral load boundary, drawn as the dashed line. This is Panel C's
# boundary, taken from `tier_binload_cut` rather than restated, so "high load"
# means one thing across the figure and the two cannot drift apart. Panel C
# sets it from the trough of a two-component Gaussian mixture on log2 load in
# the SIV Ca*Re samples; the same procedure is run on these human 10X cells
# below to check the shared cut against what this data alone would choose.
stopifnot(exists("tier_binload_cut"))
loadsplice_cut <- tier_binload_cut

# The boundary is a convention shared with Panel C, so the chunk checks it
# against what these cells alone would choose instead of assuming it. Viral
# UMIs are swept as a `>= cut` rule for calling a viremic cell splice+ and
# scored by Youden's J = sensitivity + specificity - 1. max-F1 is not used:
# splice+ prevalence among viremic HIV+ cells is low enough that F1 optimises
# precision and lands far up the load axis rather than where the two splice
# groups separate.
loadsplice_youden <- function(umis, spliced) {
  purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(umis)), function(k) {
    call <- umis >= k
    tibble(cut  = k,
           sens = sum(call & spliced) / sum(spliced),
           spec = sum(!call & !spliced) / sum(!spliced))
  }) %>% mutate(youden = sens + spec - 1)
}
loadsplice_viremic <- loadsplice_cells %>% filter(condition == "viremic")
loadsplice_sweep <- loadsplice_youden(loadsplice_viremic$viral_UMIs,
                                      loadsplice_viremic$splice_group == "splice+")

# The optimum is shallow, so the cuts within 0.01 J of it are reported with it:
# the boundary marks where the groups separate, not a sharply identified value,
# and that is what makes a cut shared with Panel C defensible here.
loadsplice_plateau <- loadsplice_sweep$cut[
  loadsplice_sweep$youden >= max(loadsplice_sweep$youden) - 0.01]
loadsplice_best <- loadsplice_sweep[which.max(loadsplice_sweep$youden), ]
loadsplice_at_cut <- loadsplice_sweep[loadsplice_sweep$cut == loadsplice_cut, ]
cat(sprintf("=== low/high load boundary: >= %d viral UMIs (Panel C's tier_binload_cut) ===\n",
            loadsplice_cut))
cat(sprintf("  at the boundary      : Youden J = %.3f, sens = %.3f, spec = %.3f\n",
            loadsplice_at_cut$youden, loadsplice_at_cut$sens, loadsplice_at_cut$spec))
cat(sprintf("  these cells' own best: >= %d UMIs, J = %.3f (cuts within 0.01 J: %d-%d)\n",
            loadsplice_best$cut, loadsplice_best$youden,
            min(loadsplice_plateau), max(loadsplice_plateau)))
cat(sprintf("  viremic splice+ cells at or above the boundary: %d of %d\n",
            sum(loadsplice_viremic$viral_UMIs >= loadsplice_cut &
                loadsplice_viremic$splice_group == "splice+"),
            sum(loadsplice_viremic$splice_group == "splice+")))
# Per-dataset optima, so a line set by the larger dataset does not hide the
# other one disagreeing with it.
print(as.data.frame(loadsplice_viremic %>% group_by(group) %>%
  summarize(own_cut = {sw <- loadsplice_youden(viral_UMIs, splice_group == "splice+")
                       sw$cut[which.max(sw$youden)]}, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(group = gsub("\n", " ", group))), row.names = FALSE)
cat("  cells at or above the pooled boundary, by condition:\n")
print(as.data.frame(loadsplice_cells %>% group_by(condition) %>%
  summarize(at_or_above = sum(viral_UMIs >= loadsplice_cut), cells = n(),
            .groups = "drop")), row.names = FALSE)

loadsplice_stats <- loadsplice_cells %>%
  group_by(condition, group) %>%
  summarize(
    n_pos      = sum(splice_group == "splice+"),
    n_neg      = sum(splice_group == "splice-"),
    max_UMIs   = max(viral_UMIs),
    median_neg = median(viral_UMIs[splice_group == "splice-"]),
    min_pos    = if (any(splice_group == "splice+"))
                   min(viral_UMIs[splice_group == "splice+"]) else NA_real_,
    # Share of splice- cells reaching the lowest load any splice+ cell of the
    # same group carries: 0 means the two groups do not overlap in load at all.
    pct_neg_at_min_pos = if (any(splice_group == "splice+") && any(splice_group == "splice-"))
                   100 * mean(viral_UMIs[splice_group == "splice-"] >= min_pos) else NA_real_,
    diff       = if (n_pos > 0 && n_neg > 0)
                   mean(viral_UMIs[splice_group == "splice+"]) -
                   mean(viral_UMIs[splice_group == "splice-"]) else NA_real_,
    p          = if (n_pos > 0 && n_neg > 0)
                   wilcox.test(viral_UMIs ~ splice_group)$p.value else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop")
cat("=== viral UMIs per cell, splice+ vs splice- ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(loadsplice_stats %>%
  mutate(across(c(median_neg, min_pos, pct_neg_at_min_pos, diff), ~ round(.x, 2)),
         p = signif(p, 2))), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nsplice+ cells on ART, by arm:\n")
print(as.data.frame(loadsplice_cells %>% filter(condition == "ART") %>%
  group_by(arm, dataset) %>%
  summarize(called = n(), splice_pos = sum(splice_group == "splice+"),
            max_UMIs = max(viral_UMIs), .groups = "drop")), row.names = FALSE)

# Boxplots are drawn from a subset rather than suppressed by alpha, so a group
# below the minimum has no box at all instead of an invisible one.
loadsplice_drawable <- function(min_cells) {
  loadsplice_cells %>% group_by(group, splice_group) %>%
    filter(n() >= min_cells) %>% ungroup()
}
loadsplice_annot <- loadsplice_stats %>%
  left_join(loadsplice_cells %>% group_by(condition, group) %>%
              summarize(y = max(viral_UMIs), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("condition", "group")) %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(is.na(diff), "no splice+",
                        sprintf("Δ = %.1f\np = %.2g", diff, p)))

loadsplice_colors <- c("splice-" = "orange", "splice+" = "purple")
loadsplice_dodge  <- position_dodge(width = 0.8)

loadsplice_plot <- ggplot(loadsplice_cells,
                          aes(x = group, y = viral_UMIs, fill = splice_group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = loadsplice_cut, linetype = "dashed",
             linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_boxplot(data = loadsplice_drawable(loadsplice_min_box),
               position = loadsplice_dodge, width = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA,
               linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(color = splice_group),
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.25, dodge.width = 0.8,
                                             seed = 1),
             size = 0.7, alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = loadsplice_annot, aes(x = group, y = y, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.3, size = 2.4, lineheight = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(. ~ condition, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = loadsplice_colors, name = NULL, drop = FALSE,
                    limits = names(loadsplice_colors)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = loadsplice_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_log10(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.22))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "viral UMIs per cell (log scale)",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste("HIV/SIV RNA+ CD4 T cells; box at n >= 5 per splice",
                                "group, points always\ndashed = low/high viral load",
                                "boundary, %d UMIs (as Panel C)"),
                          loadsplice_cut)) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom")

# cairo_pdf: the default pdf device cannot encode the Delta in the annotations
ggsave(paste0(output.dir, "PanelJ_loadVsSplice.pdf"), loadsplice_plot,
       width = 7, height = 4.2, device = cairo_pdf)
# The axis labels carry a newline so the arm sits under the dataset; that
```
